tokyo_roppongi_inakaya_higashi.gf_detail: Ask. Robatayaki grilled over charcoal and generally served seasoned (August 2026); finishes with cold green-tea soba (May 2026). Nothing is said about gluten.
tokyo_roppongi_inakaya_higashi.vegan_detail: Ask. Vegetables such as eggplant, corn, shiitake and asparagus are grilled to order (July 2026), but seasonings are not described; the rest is seafood and meat.
tokyo_roppongi_inakaya_higashi.hours_raw: Daily 17:00–23:00; closed 2–7 January (Tabelog). No printed menu or prices: you choose from the ingredients laid out in front of the counter, and several 2026 diners were shocked by the bill — e.g. kinki ¥15,000, kuruma prawn ¥6,800, about ¥20,000–50,000 a head. ¥880 appetizer charge (July 2026) and 10% service. 38 seats, all at the counter; whole-shop hire. Non-smoking. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay) and Alipay/WeChat Pay. Children and strollers welcome. Mostly overseas guests (2026 reviews).
tokyo_roppongi_inakaya_higashi.notes: [Robatayaki · Roppongi, the 1970 robata theatre with no price list] Since 1970 Roppongi Inakaya has staged robatayaki as a show: guests sit along a 38-seat counter facing a bank of fresh seafood, vegetables and meat, point at what to have, and grill masters roast it over charcoal with loud calls and pass it across on long wooden paddles. Diners in 2026 say former President Trump and Prime Minister Abe ate here and that most guests now come from overseas; diners praise the prawns, the kinki and the closing green-tea soba, and the mochi-pounding — but there are no prices on display and many were stunned by bills of ¥20,000–50,000 a head (a kinki ¥15,000, a prawn ¥6,800). The East shop; a West shop is nearby.

chef_bio.origin: Roppongi Inakaya, established 1970 (official site); East shop of two (East and West)
chef_bio.background: The official site describes Roppongi Inakaya as a robatayaki izakaya founded in 1970 (Showa 45) that has welcomed heads of state and famous guests. Reviewers in May and September 2026 say former President Trump and former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe dined here. No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.specialty: Robatayaki served on wooden paddles; kinki; kuruma prawns.

anecdotes.text: "It all starts with the classic question, "How many shrimp would you like?" and these shrimp are simply outstanding." — May 2026, business dinner.
"There’s no menu book; instead, the options are displayed on the wall and on a tray in front of you, making it a bit challenging to decide what to order." — January 2026 visit.
"Without any prices listed on the menu, it’s hard to gauge the current costs, which makes it feel like the value isn’t great." — June 2026, over ¥50,000 for two.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (roppongiinakaya.jp): 六本木田舎家は昭和45年創業の炉端焼きの居酒屋、米国大統領など各国の要人や著名人が訪れる。食べログ (店舗会員): 六本木田舎家 東店、港区六本木3-14-7 アロービル1F、都バス「Roppongi-Go-Chome」から徒歩1分、六本木駅5番出口から4分、毎日17:00〜23:00、1月2〜7日休み、サービス料10%、38席 (すべてカウンター)、貸切可、禁煙、カード・Alipay・WeChat Pay 可、子ども可。口コミ(2025年12月〜2026年9月): メニューや値段の表示がなく目の前の食材から選ぶ、炭火の炉端で焼き長いへらで渡す、キンキ15,000円、車海老6,800円、刺身盛り合わせ (小) 6,710円、お通し880円、1人20,000〜50,000円、餅つき、締めの冷たい茶そば、海外の客が多い、元大統領 Trump と元首相 Abe が訪れたという声。

cultural_comfort.note: Point-and-choose counter; mostly overseas guests (2026 reviews). Ask prices before ordering.

tokyo_hanasaki_yama_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. Lunch plates include hamburg steak with demi-glace, fresh pasta, chicken cutlet and cream stew, and the dinner signature is a seafood pie baked in a cocotte; nothing gluten-free is described. A September 2025 diner with allergies thought the butter might be blended with margarine.
tokyo_hanasaki_yama_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: every main is meat or seafood with butter, cream or cheese sauces.
tokyo_hanasaki_yama_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri lunch 11:45–13:30 and dinner 18:00–21:00; closed Saturday, Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). Lunch fills by about 12:15, with a "Full" sign on the door, a 50-minute limit and dishes that sell out (2025–26 reviews). Cash only (Tabelog; September 2026). No service or table charge; children under school age may be refused, and a ¥500 table charge applies to children who do not order; private hire for 10–12 (Tabelog). 16 seats; non-smoking (Tabelog).
tokyo_hanasaki_yama_yotsuya.notes: [French · Yotsuya, a fairy-tale bistro run by a couple] A storybook little bistro with big windows on Sanei-dōri — one diner compares it to a Studio Ghibli set — run by a couple who cook and serve home-style French. Weekday lunch is the draw: around ¥1,000 for salad, a thick potato-corn soup, rice and a main such as a demi-glace cheese hamburg with a hint of cinnamon, herb-grilled Daisen chicken or the house plate of hamburg, fresh pasta and fruit; portions are modest and the daily specials sell out, so come before 12:15. At dinner the dish to order is the seafood pie baked in a cocotte. One diner with allergies found the butter seemed blended with margarine. Cash only; weekdays only.

roles: Run by a couple (September 2025 review)
chef_bio.background: No source names the owners. "The couple running the place provided attentive service and cooking" (September 2025); "A refined lady guided me to my table" (September 2025); "a cozy French restaurant that has been around for a long time" (March 2026); a March 2025 diner who had known it for a long time found the dinner menu and prices unchanged, now open on weekdays only.
chef_bio.specialty: Lunch plates; seafood pie in a cocotte.

anecdotes.text: "The seafood pot pie is their specialty and is unforgettable in its deliciousness. It's only available during dinner." — March 2025.
"I expected a regular hamburger, but it had a subtle sweet aroma reminiscent of cinnamon, and it was absolutely delicious." — May 2026, lunch ¥1,000.
"During my previous visits around 12:15 PM, the door handle had a 'Full' sign… I finally managed to visit on my third attempt." — August 2026.

tokyo_cruz_burgers_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: beef patties, house-smoked bacon, pulled pork, cheese; the avocado and cheese burger still has a beef patty.
tokyo_cruz_burgers_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon and Thu–Sun lunch 11:30–15:30 (last order 15:00) and dinner 17:30–21:00 (last order 20:30); closed Tuesday and Wednesday; a short summer break in August (Tabelog). Reservations only for 17:30 onward; one dish and one drink per person; 2-hour limit at dinner; no strollers inside (Tabelog). Lunch fills soon after opening, with a line even on weekdays (October 2026). Order by voice or by smartphone (October 2026). 20 seats (2 at the counter, 18 at tables); non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR including PayPay (Tabelog).
tokyo_cruz_burgers_yotsuya.notes: [Burgers · Yotsuya, a Tabelog 100 burger and craft-beer bar] A small burger bar on Sanei-dōri, on Tabelog's Hamburger 100 list in 2017–2019, 2021 and 2026, that has drawn longer lines since appearing on a YouTube channel (TV producer Nobuyuki Sakuma recommends the pulled pork). The patty is hand-chopped domestic beef grilled on lava stone, steak-like in texture, in a long-fermented, toasted bun; the bacon is smoked in-house from premium pork. Favourites are the Noble Bacon Cheese, the teriyaki with egg and the dinner-only pulled-pork plate wrapped in tortillas; weekday lunch is a ¥1,680 set with fries or coleslaw and a drink. Five American-style craft beers on draft. A couple of October 2026 diners found the burgers good but not memorable. Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner or cooks. Tabelog: domestic beef patty hand-chopped and grilled on lava stone; long-fermented French-style bun; house-smoked bacon; five draft beers "carefully selected by the owner from domestic American-style craft breweries"; the pulled-pork plate "Recommended by TV producer Nobuyuki Sakuma". Tabelog Hamburger "Tabelog 100" 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2026.

anecdotes.text: "I visited after watching a video by Nobuyuki Sakuma. I had the BBQ Pulled Pork & Cheese Burger… Everything was incredibly delicious!" — October 2026.

"They are quite delicious, but there wasn't anything that would draw me back for a second visit." — October 2026.

tokyo_unten_yogashi_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. The parfaits layer sponge cake, cookies and meringue, and the case holds cream puffs, croissants and cakes; nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_unten_yogashi_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Ask. Some parfaits use a soy-milk cream, but they also hold milk ice cream, sponge and meringue, and no vegan item is named.
tokyo_unten_yogashi_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon and Thu–Sun (and holidays) 11:30–19:00 (last order 18:30); closed Tuesday and Wednesday, open when those are holidays (Tabelog). No reservations; order and pay at the register, then sit (July 2026). 10 seats at five tables for two; non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog). Cream puffs can sell out by evening (October 2026). Takeaway cakes, baked goods and cookie tins; LINE notices (2026 reviews). Opened 22 December 2023 (Tabelog).
tokyo_unten_yogashi_yotsuya.notes: [Sweets · Yotsuya, an Okinawan pastry café in the backstreets] The Tokyo outpost of an Okinawa pastry shop, tucked into a residential lane a short walk past the State Guest House, with ten seats for eating in. Its idea is sweets that make everyone glad, down to cookies baked with the sugarcane fibre left after juicing. The parfaits are the reason to sit down: passion fruit layered with crunchy and juicy textures, or a purple sweet potato Mont Blanc with soy-milk cream and shikuwasa jelly, alongside a carrot cake with peanut cream and a passion-fruit shortcake. Cream puffs sell out by evening. 2026 diners praise the warm, smiling staff; one found the air conditioning strong. Order at the register; closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 22 December 2023 (Tabelog); the second shop of ペストリーうんてん, whose other shop is in 豊見城, Okinawa (official site).
chef_bio.background: Official site (unten.store): ペストリーうんてん makes sweets on the concept of "「うれしい」がめぐるお菓子", caring for health and the environment; its Meguru cookies use sugarcane left after juicing, which would otherwise be burned; shops in 豊見城市平良76-1 (Okinawa) and 若葉1-16-7 (Yotsuya); an online shop and a farm page. No source names the bakers.
chef_bio.philosophy: "「うれしい」がめぐるお菓子" — sweets that pass happiness around, to growers and eaters alike (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Parfaits; carrot cake with peanut cream; cream puffs.

anecdotes.text: "The top layer of soy milk cream was subtly sweet, with a strong soy milk flavor… there were fine shikuwasa jelly pieces mixed in." — September 2026, purple sweet potato Mont Blanc parfait ¥1,500.
"The air conditioning inside was quite strong… for someone like me who gets cold easily, having a light cardigan might be a good idea." — July 2026.
"I was surprised by such warm hospitality for just a takeout customer." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (unten.store): ペストリーうんてん、「うれしい」がめぐるお菓子がコンセプト、身体や環境にも配慮、めぐるクッキーには搾汁後のサトウキビ、豊見城店 (沖縄県豊見城市平良76-1) と四ツ谷店 (新宿区若葉1-16-7)、オンラインショップ。食べログ: うんてん洋菓子店 四ツ谷店、洋菓子・カフェ、若葉1-16-7、四ツ谷駅から徒歩7分、月・木〜日・祝11:30〜19:00 (L.O.18:30)、火・水休み (祝日は営業)、予約不可、10席、禁煙、カード・電子マネー・QR 可、テイクアウト、2023年12月22日オープン。口コミ(2026年6月〜10月): パッションフルーツのパフェ1,700円、紅芋のモンブランパフェ1,500円 (豆乳クリーム、シークヮーサーのジュレ)、キャロットケーキ780円、パッションフルーツのショートケーキ980円、シュークリーム、めぐるクッキー、レジで注文して先に会計、スタッフが親切、冷房が強め。

tokyo_yorozuya_okagesan_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the shop asks guests to state allergies and dislikes when reserving (Tabelog, quoting its website). The omakase is dashi-led fish cooking with soy-based seasonings, satsuma-age and an okara dish; nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_yorozuya_okagesan_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-centred omakase built on dashi.
tokyo_yorozuya_okagesan_yotsuya.hours_raw: Tue–Sat from 18:00, last entry 19:00, closing about 22:00; closed Sunday, Monday and holidays (Tabelog). Reservation only, by the shop (no travel agencies); single diners only on the day and not when only a table for two is free; the shop calls the day before to confirm; cancellation fee (Tabelog). Often fully booked; walk-ins turned away (May and July 2026). Chef's-choice course only, ¥8,000 + tax (¥8,800) since 1 October 2025, with optional extras; most guests add dishes, and with drinks the bill is about ¥14,000 (Tabelog). 17 seats: 7 at the counter, 10 at tables; non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
tokyo_yorozuya_okagesan_yotsuya.notes: [Izakaya · Yotsuya, a sake lover's omakase in a basement] A 17-seat basement izakaya near Yotsuya-sanchome, on Tabelog's Izakaya 100 list four times, that runs only on reservations and a chef's-choice course (¥8,800 plus whatever you add, about ¥14,000 with drinks). Dishes come one after another to go with sake: seasonal greens in dashi, sashimi such as kinmedai under karasumi or charcoal-seared katsuo, aji namero, okara with sakura shrimp, simmered anago, and always, at the end, a soft salt rice ball that diners rave about. The staff choose sake to match and let you pick your cup. The owner greets each table, and regulars book the counter privately. One February 2026 diner found nothing on the menu remarkable but praised the care. Book well ahead; closed Sundays, Mondays and holidays.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner. Reviews: "the owner personally came to greet us" (April 2026); "the owner greeted each of us individually while handing out business cards. A lively female staff member carefully explained the course details written on the blackboard" (July 2026); "reflecting the warm personality of the owner" (June 2026). Tabelog: Izakaya "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2022; Izakaya EAST "Tabelog 100" 2024, 2025; chef's-choice course only, ¥8,000 + tax from 1 October 2025 (quoting the shop's website).
chef_bio.specialty: Omakase with sake; salt rice ball.

anecdotes.text: "Don't underestimate the simple salt rice ball served at the end. It was incredibly soft and fluffy, completely changing my perception of rice balls." — April 2026.
"I really appreciate that they change the ochoko (sake cups) for each type of sake." — March 2026.
"While there isn't anything particularly noteworthy on the menu, every detail of the service is handled with care." — February 2026.

tokyo_milk_stand_okachimachi.gf_detail: GF — ask: plain bottled milks have no wheat, but flavoured milks, coffee milk and drinking yogurt are not described, and there is no gluten-free statement.
tokyo_milk_stand_okachimachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a milk bar — cow's milk, coffee milk and drinking yogurt.
tokyo_milk_stand_okachimachi.hours_raw: Mon–Thu 11:25–14:40; Fri 11:25–13:40; Sat–Sun 9:45–18:00; closed public holidays (Tabelog; same hours quoted in an October 2025 review). A June 2026 visitor says it usually opens at noon and is often closed when passing. A standing counter (4 spaces) right outside the JR Okachimachi North Exit ticket gate. Drink on the spot and return the bottle. No cards; e-money accepted. Hot milk in the cold months.
tokyo_milk_stand_okachimachi.notes: [Milk bar · Okachimachi Station, regional milk at the ticket gate] A tiny standing milk counter right outside the North Exit gate of JR Okachimachi Station, run by 大沢牛乳, the dairy dealer behind the famous milk stand on Akihabara's Sōbu Line platform. It sells bottled local milks from across Japan — Kazusa, Azumino, Sunflower milk from Kōchi — plus coffee milk and drinking yogurt for under ¥200; you drink on the spot and hand back the bottle, and in winter the milk can be warmed. Tourists sometimes stop to watch (September 2026). Hours are short and odd on weekdays (roughly 11:25 to 14:40, shorter on Fridays) and longer at weekends; closed on holidays.

chef_bio.background: Run by 大沢牛乳 (president 大沢一彦), which also runs the ミルクショップ酪 milk stand on the JR Akihabara Sōbu Line platform; from around 2000 it began stocking regional milks, now from about 15 dairies; the Okachimachi stand is popular with tourists from China and Korea (乗りものニュース, 6 March 2023).

anecdotes.text: "I enjoyed the limited edition Kazusa Milk for JPY 160, which was warmed in hot water." — March 2026.
"You drink it on the spot and return the bottle afterward." — September 2026, drinking yogurt.
"It's outside the ticket gate, and the hours are super tight (and quite specific too, haha)!" — October 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: ミルクスタンド 御徒町店、上野5 JR御徒町駅北口改札前、月〜木11:25〜14:40、金11:25〜13:40、土日9:45〜18:00、祝日休み、予約不可、立ち飲みカウンター4席、禁煙、カード不可・電子マネー可。乗りものニュース (2023年3月6日、古橋龍一): 秋葉原駅総武線ホームの「ミルクショップ酪」を運営する大沢牛乳、社長の大沢一彦さん、2000年頃からご当地牛乳を扱い、全国15社ほどのメーカーの牛乳 (福島の酪王牛乳、千葉のかずさ牛乳、岐阜の飛騨牛乳、高知のひまわり牛乳)、御徒町駅の大沢牛乳のミルクスタンドは中国・韓国の観光客に人気。口コミ (2024年8月〜2026年9月): 安曇野の牛乳180円、温めたかずさ牛乳160円、ひまわり牛乳、低温殺菌のコーヒー牛乳、飲むヨーグルト、その場で飲んで瓶を返す、昼ごろ開くことが多い。

cultural_comfort.note: Point at the bottle on the menu board; staff open it for you.

tokyo_thai_sky_kitchen_ueno.gf_detail: GF — ask: rice-based Thai dishes, but stir-fries use oyster and soy sauce and there are fried spring rolls and wontons; nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_thai_sky_kitchen_ueno.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: stir-fried water spinach and other vegetable dishes are on the menu, but those are seasoned with oyster sauce, and no vegan dish is named.
tokyo_thai_sky_kitchen_ueno.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–15:00 (last order 14:30) and 17:00–22:30 (last order 22:00) (Tabelog). Weekday lunch sets only; weekends and holidays serve the regular menu all day (Tabelog notice; July 2026). Reservations taken; fully booked by early afternoon on an October 2026 Saturday. Some dishes unavailable on a July 2026 evening. 20 seats. Non-smoking. Cards, e-money and QR. English menu and English-speaking staff. Take-out and delivery.
tokyo_thai_sky_kitchen_ueno.notes: [Thai · Ueno, a bright Thai dining room above Nakachō-dōri] A second-floor Thai restaurant on a corner of Ueno's Nakachō-dōri, with big windows that make it bright and resort-like at lunch. The kitchen, led by a chef from Bangkok per the listing, covers the classics — gapao rice, green and massaman curries (¥1,280), yum woon sen, coconut soup — and stronger dishes like soft-shell crab curry, tom sep pork-bone soup and Thai sausage. Weekday lunch has set menus; weekends are à la carte all day, and Saturday afternoons can be fully booked. Most 2026 diners found it authentic; one in September 2026 found the seafood soup short on seafood, and some dishes were unavailable one July evening.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing (official information), cooking by a top chef from Bangkok. A notice on the listing signs off "Thai Sky Kitchen (Ueno & Okachimachi)". No source names the chef.

tokyo_baton_motoasakusa.notes: [Pudding & café · Shin-Okachimachi, custard puddings and soufflé pancakes] A bright, simple pudding shop and café between Shin-Okachimachi and Inaricho, open since 2017. The draw is a long line of custard puddings made with carefully chosen eggs and vanilla beans (¥340–510): the house Inochi pudding, one made with pale rice-fed yolks and black-sugar sauce, plus matcha, hojicha, café-au-lait and pistachio. Sit down for fluffy soufflé pancakes (whipped to order, so each takes a while) or a crisp egg tart and coffee for ¥700; there is keema curry at lunch and a buffet on Fridays. Order and pay by phone. Open daily per Tabelog, including Sundays, when many nearby places are closed (May 2026).

tokyo_hotei_shitaya.notes: [Izakaya · Iriya, a 1976 fish izakaya with monkfish hot pot] A calm, long-established izakaya on a back street near Iriya Station, in business since 1976, with a counter, a few tables and a raised tatami area — reminding one reviewer of a small kaiseki restaurant. Winter is monkfish season: the anko nabe, finished with rice porridge, is what it is known for. At lunch it fills up for generous set meals at about ¥1,000–1,300: tender pork kakuni, juicy salt-seasoned kara-age, a thick-cut katsuo bowl, or a sashimi set, each with miso soup and pickles. In the evening, sashimi, crab-miso tofu and whole squid go with beer and sake. Pay by cash or PayPay. Closed Sundays and holidays.

tokyo_huit_ningyocho.notes: [Bistro · Ningyocho, natural wine, junmai sake and vegetables on Amazake Yokocho] A fifth-floor bistro in the KYOE PLAZA dining building, pairing natural wines and junmai sake with vegetable-forward cooking from partner farms. The master is a certified sommelier (October 2026). The bargain is the ¥3,800 food-only course: six small plates and a chewy homemade rosemary bread that diners rave about, from wild-boar rillettes and kombu-cured carpaccio to salt-koji pork with tonnato. Lunch starts at ¥1,400, and weekends run straight through from noon. Staff are warm, chatting even with children (July 2026); portions can feel small to big eaters. Dinner is about two hours, and non-drinkers pay ¥500 after 15:00.

tokyo_ryuen_ningyocho.notes: [Kaiseki · Ningyocho, a monthly-changing Japanese counter with a devoted following] An eight-seat Japanese counter on the seventh floor of KYOE PLAZA, open since 2021 and a Tabelog Japanese-cuisine 100 pick in 2023 and 2025. The young chef Noro writes a new menu each month: sea urchin with winter melon and abalone, a Chateaubriand cutlet with matsutake, sake-marinated hairy crab, a small hot pot, then a rice course with leftovers packed to take home. Pairings lean on carefully chosen sake, with Burgundy when the dish calls for it. Regulars return monthly, one for a 21st visit (July 2026), and several compare it favourably with starred restaurants. The omakase is about ¥27,000–¥29,700. Book well ahead, arrive on time, and skip the perfume.

tokyo_lappartamento_di_naoki_ningyocho.notes: [Italian · Ningyocho, a wood-fired counter that moved from Azabu-Juban] An Italian counter on the fourth floor of KYOE PLAZA, where chef Naoki Yokoe moved in 2021 after ten years in Azabu-Juban, adding a wood-fired oven the old shop lacked. Smoke runs through everything, down to the ice cream, and the pasta comes after the main as small servings of three or more kinds, made in front of you. The kitchen is a one-chef show, so the chef talks once dessert arrives (May 2026). A Tabelog Italian 100 pick in 2023 and 2025. Adults only; book via Tabelog, Instagram or LINE.

tokyo_oryori_kokoroba_ningyocho.notes: [Kaiseki · Ningyocho, a one-person kaiseki counter in hinoki] A six-seat kaiseki counter on the third floor of KYOE PLAZA, built in Kiso hinoki and cedar like a tea room, and run entirely by one owner who cooks, explains and serves. Courses start with a clean, strong ichiban dashi and move through Toyosu fish, a hamo clear soup and wagyu with noodles, with a sake pairing at ¥550 a cup. Lunch is the way in: an oyakodon course for about ¥5,000. Several 2026 diners say it now holds a Michelin star. Because one person does everything, the owner is often in the back, and some evenings had only one or two parties (April, June 2026). One June 2026 diner found the portions a little small.

roles: Owner, cooking and serving single-handed (Tabelog shop text; "a one-person operation", June 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Opened 20 August 2022 (Tabelog). Per the Tabelog shop text: a tea-room-style counter of Kiso hinoki and cedar; ingredients from Toyosu Market; tableware by artisans from across Japan; the owner's greeting aims for "a comfortable home-like atmosphere that is both soft and dignified". Horse ornaments reflect the name (August 2026). Reviews from June, July and September 2026 describe it as Michelin-starred; an April 2026 review calls it Michelin Guide-listed.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Subtle yet extravagant" Japanese elegance in cuisine, decor and hospitality (owner's greeting, Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "Since it's a one-person operation, the chef is often in the back, making it hard to see" — June 2026.
"The first dish is the ichiban dashi, featuring a robust bonito flavor that is free of any impurities" — August 2026.
"Since it was a Sunday night, there was only one staff member, and I was the only customer for a while." — September 2026.

cultural_comfort.note: Reservation only; smart casual; the owner explains each dish.

tokyo_oyoge_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. The batter is described as Western-pastry style with almond flour and brown sugar (September 2026), but its full ingredients are not given; assume wheat until the shop confirms.
tokyo_oyoge_roppongi.vegan_detail: Ask. Fillings include butter, cream cheese, custard and chocolate; the batter's ingredients are not given. Tabelog lists vegetarian options.
tokyo_oyoge_roppongi.hours_raw: Daily 10:30–23:00; hours may change (Tabelog). Takeout only. Cashless only — no cash (Tabelog); cards, IC/e-money and PayPay. Pets and children welcome. English menu. Opened 1 March 2020 (Tabelog).
tokyo_oyoge_roppongi.notes: [Sweets · Roppongi, "taiyaki" shaped like sardines and clams] A takeout shop two minutes from Roppongi Station, open 10:30 am to 11 pm, that asks why taiyaki must be sea bream and bakes sardines, horse mackerel, clams and Spanish mackerel instead. The batter is closer to a financier — almond flour and brown sugar, crisp outside and moist inside — around fillings like red bean with cream cheese, salted butter, salted melon cream or chocolate, with flavours that change with the season. Diners in 2026 loved the look and found them good as gifts; some thought the batter thick and filling, others a little dry. Cashless only.

chef_bio.background: Opened 1 March 2020 (Tabelog). A September 2026 diner describes the concept as "a taiyaki shop without sea bream" and notes a batter deliberately developed with Western-pastry ingredients. No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Why does it have to be sea bream?" (as reported by a September 2026 diner).

anecdotes.text: "This is a unique shop called "a taiyaki shop without sea bream," where the showcase features sardines, horse mackerel, and clams instead of the traditional sea bream." — September 2026, an-butter.
"The batter is very delicious and differs from the typical taiyaki batter; it has a texture similar to that of a madeleine, making it quite tasty." — October 2026.
"The dough was quite thick, giving it a somewhat dry texture with not much flavor." — July 2026, BOX set ¥1,164.

tokyo_hayato_roppongi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a set omakase that includes dumplings, a bonito cutlet, noodles and a pasta (September–October 2026).
tokyo_hayato_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: shark fin in collagen soup, seafood, pork and foie gras.
tokyo_hayato_roppongi.hours_raw: Two seatings, everyone starting together: from 18:00 and from 21:00; please be punctual — late guests join the course where it is (Tabelog). Opening days are not listed. Reservations through the OMAKASE site (Tabelog); a 2-year wait was reported in October 2026, and 18 months in another October 2026 review. Omakase ¥49,500 (September–October 2026); drinks are market-priced and expensive (October 2026). 10% service charge. 8 seats. Non-smoking. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR. Opened 27 August 2018 (Tabelog).
tokyo_hayato_roppongi.notes: [Chinese · Roppongi, an 8-seat nouvelle-Chinese chef's table with a two-year wait] A basement counter of eight where chef Toshiyuki Yoshida — trained at SENSE in the Mandarin Oriental Tokyo and on a restaurant opening on the Champs-Élysées — cooks a Cantonese-based omakase that changes every two months, plated on custom tableware under spotlights. Diners in 2026 rank the hammerhead shark fin in collagen soup as the best shark fin ever, and remember the matsutake "aroma bomb" dim sum, a straw-smoked bonito cutlet and a mushroom cream pasta among the finales. Tabelog Award Silver 2024–2026. Booking is through OMAKASE and runs 18 months to two years ahead; the course is ¥49,500 and drinks are expensive.

roles: Chef (Tabelog shop text)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: born in Utsunomiya, Tochigi; after high school moved to Tokyo and worked at upscale Chinese restaurants and at SENSE, Mandarin Oriental Tokyo; then went to France with SENSE's head chef of the time to open a restaurant on the Champs-Élysées in Paris; aims for innovative dishes using a wide range of techniques, not only Chinese. A September 2026 diner notes the chef cannot eat cheese and makes the closing pasta egg-yolk-based. Regulars call the shop "Toshi's world" (October 2026). An October 2026 reviewer refers to the "Hasegawa Minoru chain" when commenting on drink prices. The Tabelog Award: Bronze 2022 and 2023, Silver 2024, 2025 and 2026; Tabelog Chinese 100 (Tokyo) 2021, 2023, 2024, 2026. Opened 27 August 2018.
chef_bio.philosophy: A chef's table to enjoy with all five senses (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Hammerhead shark fin in collagen soup.

anecdotes.text: "It featured hammerhead shark fin in a collagen-rich soup—so rich and delicious!" — September 2026, pairing course.
"The course menu changes every two months, so I can never predict what to expect." — September 2026.
"It's surprising that drinks cost more than the food—this isn’t a cabaret club…" — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 隼、港区六本木4-4-2 ヒルサイドパレス六本木B1F、六本木駅7番出口から徒歩2分、18時からと21時からの一斉スタートの2部制、予約は OMAKASE、サービス料10%、8席、禁煙、カード可、2018年8月27日オープン、The Tabelog Award 2022・2023 Bronze、2024・2025・2026 Silver、中国料理 TOKYO 百名店 2021・2023・2024・2026。店の紹介: 料理長 吉田隼之 (Utsunomiya 生まれ、都内の高級中国料理店と SENSE で経験を積み、Paris の Champs-Élysées の店の立ち上げにも関わる)、乾燥ふかひれをじっくり戻した厚いふかひれ。口コミ(2026年7月〜10月): おまかせ49,500円、2か月ごとに変わるコース、撞木鮫のふかひれとコラーゲンのスープ、松茸の香りの点心、藁で燻した戻り鰹のカツ、締めの麺と炒飯とクリームパスタ、飲み物が高いという声、予約は2年待ちという声。

cultural_comfort.note: Set omakase at a counter with the chef explaining each dish; book via OMAKASE.

tokyo_shifang_cai_yoshida_roppongi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: xiao long bao, spring rolls, dim sum and noodles are central to the menu (2026 reviews).
tokyo_shifang_cai_yoshida_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pigeon, chicken, black pork, seafood and shark fin.
tokyo_shifang_cai_yoshida_roppongi.hours_raw: Tue–Sat, holidays and days before/after holidays 17:00–22:30 (last order 22:00); closed Sundays and Mondays; book any time from 17:00; a two-hour limit when busy (Tabelog). Order the fried pigeon by the day before. 5% service charge, no cover. 20 seats: 6 at the counter and tables; private hire up to 20. Non-smoking. Cards, e-money and QR (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay and others).
tokyo_shifang_cai_yoshida_roppongi.notes: [Chinese · Roppongi, Hayato's à la carte sister upstairs] A chic, brown-toned room of 20 seats one floor above Hayato, opened in November 2024 as its sister and selected for the Tabelog Chinese 100 in 2026. Unlike the omakase below, you mostly order à la carte: the "Pekichiki" — chicken done like Peking duck, with candy that crackles in the mouth — a shark-fin xiao long bao with a startlingly rich soup, Kirishima black-pork char siu, and a whole fragrant fried pigeon eaten with a glove. Diners in 2026 found it stylish but relaxed, good for dates and business, with a strong wine list. Courses from the ¥22,000 "Gokigen" with shark fin.

chef_bio.chef_name: Hiroaki Yoshida (as written in an October 2026 review)
roles: Owner-chef (October 2026 review)
chef_bio.origin: Formerly of Seifuro in Yokohama (October 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: An October 2026 diner writes that the restaurant opened in November 2024 as a sister of Hayato, and that the owner, chef Hiroaki Yoshida, comes from the long-established "Seifuro" in Yokohama and has been head chef at "Yasai Hanten" and "Chuka Bar Sawada". The Tabelog menu names a xiao long bao after "Toshi", Hayato's chef Toshiyuki Yoshida. Tabelog Chinese 100 (Tokyo) 2026.
chef_bio.specialty: Pekichiki; shark-fin xiao long bao; fried pigeon.

anecdotes.text: "This luxurious dish uses shark fin, and what surprised me the most was the richness of the soup." — October 2026, Toshi's Rich Xiao Long Bao ¥1,760.
"Eating with a gloved left hand allows you to savor every bit, even the brain." — September 2026, fragrant fried pigeon.
"At Sifon Choi Yoshida, the focus is on a la carte dishes rather than set courses." — October 2026.

tokyo_sushi_ryuma_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. A sushi course with soy-marinated tuna, Saikyo-miso cream cheese and dobin-mushi (2026 reviews); nothing is said about gluten.
tokyo_sushi_ryuma_roppongi.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegan and vegetarian options, but no vegan dishes are described; the courses are fish, shellfish and crab, and the dobin-mushi broth has been made with soft-shelled turtle (August 2026).
tokyo_sushi_ryuma_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Wed, Sat, Sun, holidays and days before/after holidays: 12:00–15:00 and 17:00–23:00; Thu and Fri: 17:00–23:00 (Tabelog). 10% service charge. 22 seats: 9 at the counter and private rooms for 6 and 8 (up to 20). Non-smoking. Children only if able to eat the adult menu. BYO possible. Cards, iD/QUICPay and QR (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay and others). In a nightlife building near Midtown (September 2026).
tokyo_sushi_ryuma_roppongi.notes: [Sushi · Roppongi, playful "double" nigiri with an entertaining chef] A calm sushi counter of nine with two wood-panelled private rooms, on the third floor of a lively building by Tokyo Midtown. The ¥28,600 course opens with matsutake dobin-mushi, moves through aged fish — five-day kohada from Amakusa, week-aged hirame and shima-aji — and then the house twists: a kuruma prawn hiding a sweet shrimp, squid over sea urchin, ōtoro with chopped toro inside, an overflowing purple-urchin gunkan. Diners in 2026 come back as much for the chef, who keeps the counter laughing and explains every piece, as for the sushi. Lunch most days; private rooms for business dinners.

chef_bio.background: The Tabelog shop text says the chefs have trained at many renowned restaurants. Diners in 2026 describe a friendly, humorous chef who explains each piece and keeps the counter laughing. No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.philosophy: Traditional Edomae sushi in harmony with creative sushi (Tabelog shop text).

anecdotes.text: "To my surprise, the chef was incredibly entertaining, keeping everyone laughing throughout the evening." — September 2026, Premium Sushi Course ¥28,600.
"Next was Kohada, aged for five days from Amakusa." — October 2026.
"I was amazed by the sushi that allowed us to enjoy two types of toppings in one piece, like squid paired with sea urchin and shrimp with sweet shrimp." — October 2026.

tokyo_sushi_yasumitsu_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask when booking. An omakase of sushi and small dishes with soy-based seasonings, a matsutake clear soup and a matcha ice-cream monaka to finish; nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_sushi_yasumitsu_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish, shellfish and crab omakase.
tokyo_sushi_yasumitsu_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Sat two seatings, 17:30–20:00 (last drinks 19:30) and 20:30–23:00 (last drinks 22:30); also open on the last Sunday of the month, closing the Monday after; closed Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). Reservation only, by phone 10:00–15:00; change or cancel at least two days ahead (Tabelog). Hard to book; regulars rebook a year ahead (December 2025, September 2026). Cash only: card payment is suspended (Tabelog). 14 seats: 8 at the counter and a private room for 6; non-smoking (Tabelog). About ¥30,000–40,000 a head with sake; omakase ¥34,100 in October 2026.
tokyo_sushi_yasumitsu_yotsuya.notes: [Sushi · Yotsuya, a second-generation counter in a residential lane] Down a lane of houses too narrow for cars, a 14-seat sushi shop that Yasuhide Watanuki took over from the chef's father, whose neighbourhood sushi bar was Kouraku Sushi, and turned into a hard-to-book omakase (Tabelog Bronze 2026). The chef fishes, travels to markets and producers, and builds the year around sea urchin in summer and crab in winter: a tasting of three uni, kobako crab in December, and in autumn 2026 Nagano matsutake in a clear soup between nigiri on red-vinegar rice. Diners praise the chef's warmth as much as the fish. Two seatings a night, cash only, booked by phone; expect about ¥35,000 a head.

roles: Head chef, second generation (reviews: "Chef Yasuhide Watanuki"; "the second generation to take over the family business, originally known as Kouraku Sushi")
chef_bio.origin: Second generation of a neighbourhood sushi shop formerly called Kouraku Sushi (October 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.background: Per an October 2026 review: "The head chef, Mr. Watanuki, is the second generation to take over the family business, originally known as Kouraku Sushi"; [the chef] "visits various fish markets", travels to taste sushi and meet producers. Tabelog Award Bronze 2026; Sushi TOKYO "Tabelog 100" 2022, 2025. No source gives the chef's name in kanji.
chef_bio.philosophy: Honouring the family shop while pursuing the chef's own sushi (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "In summer, it's a sea urchin tasting, and in winter, it's crab, but what do they serve in autumn?" — September 2026, a 26th visit.
"Nestled in the middle of a residential area filled with single-family homes, you have to walk down narrow streets where cars cannot pass to reach the restaurant." — September 2026.
"I was surprised when the first dish served was the Kōbako crab… But this was just the prologue." — December 2025.

tokyo_shio_tsukemen_toka_yotsuya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles in salt, soy or seafood dipping broths; boiled gyoza on the side. The listing says allergy information is available.
tokyo_shio_tsukemen_toka_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken and seafood broths, chashu.
tokyo_shio_tsukemen_toka_yotsuya.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–22:00, open year-round (official shop page); Tabelog gives 11:00–23:00. Ticket machine at the entrance (2026 reviews). Reservations possible, one noodle dish per person (Tabelog). 12 seats, mostly a counter of 10; non-smoking; children welcome (Tabelog; August 2026). No cards; Suica and other e-money, PayPay (Tabelog). Opened 28 August 2019 (Tabelog).
tokyo_shio_tsukemen_toka_yotsuya.notes: [Ramen · Yotsuya, a light salt tsukemen on Shinjuku-dōri] A 12-seat counter shop from the company behind the 鯛塩そば灯花 shops, devoted to salt tsukemen: chewy straight noodles beside a clear golden dipping broth of chicken and seafood, with yuzu pepper on the rim, kombu soba-yu to stretch the broth, and a spoonful of rice to drop in at the end. For a heavier bowl there is a rich seafood tsukemen, plus a soy version and a nostalgic soy chuka soba. Diners in 2026 found the shio broth light but full of umami and the grilled chashu excellent; one thought the soy tsukemen just okay. Buy a ticket at the door; open every day until 22:00.

chef_bio.background: Run by 株式会社グッドヌードルイノベーション, 四谷4-7 (official site), which also runs the 鯛塩そば灯花 brand (a new shop opened in Chofu on 15 October 2026, per its news page). No source names the cooks; an August 2026 diner noticed only women in the kitchen that day. Tabelog lists allergy information as available.

anecdotes.text: "The dish was refreshingly light yet packed with umami… After finishing the noodles, I added kombu soba-yu (noodle water) to the broth to enjoy it even more." — August 2026, shio tsukemen with flavoured egg.
「鶏ベースの塩かな？透明な黄金色のスープは見た目より濃厚。」 — August 2026, a Sunday.
"I tried the soy sauce tsukemen, but it was just okay… I should have gone for the shio tsukemen instead." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (ramen-toka.com): 塩つけ麺 灯花、四谷2-11 龍文堂ビル1F、11:00〜22:00、年中無休、12席、淡麗鶏塩そば、塩つけ麺、濃厚魚介つけ麺、水ギョウザ、昆布そば湯割り、追い飯茶漬け、運営は株式会社グッドヌードルイノベーション、鯛塩そば灯花も展開 (2026年10月に調布店オープン)。食べログ: 塩つけ麺は鶏と魚介の繊細な香りと特製塩だれのキレ、柚子胡椒、醤油つけ麺はわさび、11:00〜23:00、12席、禁煙、カード不可、電子マネー・PayPay 可、アレルギー表示あり、2019年8月28日オープン。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 塩つけ麺990円、透明な黄金色のスープは見た目より濃厚、もちもちのストレート麺、炙りチャーシュー、昆布そば湯、追い飯、券売機、醤油つけ麺は普通だったという声。

cultural_comfort.note: Ticket machine at the door; a card explains how to eat the tsukemen (October 2026).

tokyo_tiphareth_coffee_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. Coffee is the focus; the food is sandwiches, coffee pudding, coffee jelly and other desserts, not described for gluten.
tokyo_tiphareth_coffee_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Ask. Black hand-drip and cold-brew coffee are plant-only; lattes, pudding, cream-cheese sandwiches and ice cream are dairy, and no plant milk is mentioned.
tokyo_tiphareth_coffee_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 8:30–19:00; Sat and holidays 8:30–17:00; closed Sunday (Tabelog), though one diner visited on a Sunday at 12:30 (June 2026). 20 seats: five tables for two on the ground floor and a counter of 6 in a loft upstairs; non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB), Suica and QR (Tabelog). Takeaway; online shop for beans (Tabelog). Opened 1 October 2023 (Tabelog).
tokyo_tiphareth_coffee_yotsuya.notes: [Café · Yotsuya, a roastery café with a loft] A minimalist, mid-century-style café on Shinjuku-dōri whose roaster by the door scents the street from 8:30 in the morning. Pick a hand-drip coffee from the day's beans, dark to light (with decaf and sometimes a Geisha), or a cold brew, and pair it with the coffee pudding or coffee jelly with ice cream; there are breakfast sandwiches such as espresso nuts with cream cheese. The tall ground floor has a handful of tables, and a narrow loft upstairs has counter seats with a view. 2026 diners call it calm and friendly; one found the tables close together and took away instead, and a regular noticed prices have risen since opening.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner or roaster. Tabelog lists an online bean shop (tipharethshp.base.shop).

anecdotes.text: "You can choose from hand-dripped coffee options: dark roast, medium roast, and light roast. They even offer specialty Geisha coffee." — March 2026, early morning.
"Surprisingly, the affogato is cheaper than the iced coffee and comes with two scoops of vanilla." — June 2026.
"Although the ceiling was high, the seating was quite close together… so I decided to take out my order." — September 2026.

tokyo_toranoko_coffee_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. The signature egg pudding is a firm, old-style custard and may contain no flour, but nothing is labelled; Basque cheesecake and other bakes are also sold.
tokyo_toranoko_coffee_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Ask. Black coffee, hot or iced, is plant-only; the desserts are egg and dairy and no plant milk is mentioned.
tokyo_toranoko_coffee_yotsuya.hours_raw: Daily 10:30–18:00; closing days not fixed (Tabelog). Weekday reservations; at weekends and holidays only when you are first on the waiting list (Tabelog). One drink per person, 90-minute limit (Tabelog). Order and pick up at the counter (September 2026). 10 seats: a counter of 6 and two tables for two; non-smoking; strollers welcome (Tabelog; October 2026). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog). Takeaway coffee, beans and drip bags (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Opened 22 October 2017 (Tabelog).
tokyo_toranoko_coffee_yotsuya.notes: [Café · Yotsuya, a roaster café and its firm pudding] A small coffee shop down a side street near Yotsuya-sanchome, filled with the smell of beans from the big direct-fire roaster inside and sacks of green coffee by the counter. Tell the cheerful owner whether you like acidity or bitterness and several beans are set out for you to sniff before your hand-drip cup is brewed; iced café latte and the coffee of the day are the regulars' standbys. The thing to eat is the egg pudding, firm and old-fashioned, rich in egg and not too sweet, or a Basque cheesecake. Ten seats, regulars chatting at the counter, a 90-minute limit, and beans to take home.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner. Reviews describe "the kind service from the owner" (August 2026), an owner with "a surprisingly youthful vibe" (September 2026), "the owner had a cheerful smile… a detailed explanation from the owner" (October 2026), and staff who set out several beans to smell when you name a flavour (March 2026). An October 2026 reviewer tags it "Top 100 Cafes 2026".

anecdotes.text: "When you express your preference for flavors like acidity or bitterness, the staff presents several types of beans right in front of you. Being able to choose while smelling the aromas is an irresistible experience for coffee lovers." — March 2026.
"The pudding was the classic firm type, reminiscent of the old days. There were also a few books on the counter." — September 2026.
"I ordered today's hot coffee (JPY 590) and 200g of Toranoko Blend coffee beans (JPY 1980)." — October 2026, an 11th visit.

tokyo_ino_cantonese_takase_horidome.gf_detail: Ask when booking — the shop may decline bookings with wide-ranging allergies (Tabelog). Courses include dim sum, spring rolls, noodles and soy-based sauces (2026 reviews).
tokyo_ino_cantonese_takase_horidome.vegan_detail: Not vegan: seafood-centred Cantonese courses with meat dishes and Jinhua-ham soups.
tokyo_ino_cantonese_takase_horidome.hours_raw: Mon, Thu and Fri 17:30–22:30 (last entry 20:30); Sat and Sun 12:00–15:00 (last entry 13:00) and 17:30–22:30 (last entry 20:30); closed Tue and Wed (Tabelog). Reservations; wide-ranging allergies or dislikes may mean a booking is declined, and requests cannot be taken after arrival; late arrival may mean courses are cut short (Tabelog). Cards; no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). 18 seats: 8 at the counter, 3 tables for 6, a private room for 4 (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Opened August 2022 (June 2026 review).
tokyo_ino_cantonese_takase_horidome.notes: [Cantonese · Horidome-cho, refined seafood Cantonese from a former hotel head chef] The independent restaurant of Kenichi Takase, for seven years the first head chef of SENSE at the Mandarin Oriental Tokyo, opened in 2022 near Ningyocho and a Tabelog Chinese 100 pick in 2023, 2024 and 2026. The courses, renewed every two months, are light and seafood-led: Hong Kong-style steamed grouper, double-boiled soups, and the signature shrimp in a fresh mango mayonnaise. The Chinese tea is praised as specialist-grade. Weekend lunch at ¥9,680 is the easier way in; dinner runs from about ¥14,300. One April 2025 diner found it no more than polished hotel Chinese, while a September 2026 visitor ranked it among the best Chinese food ever eaten. A June 2026 reviewer says it holds a Michelin star.

roles: Owner-chef ("Fully Independent Store by Experienced Owner Kenichi Takase", Tabelog shop text)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: first head chef of SENSE at the Mandarin Oriental Tokyo for seven years; opened Cantonese Yan Ken Takase and Ginza Chuka Takase before this fully independent restaurant. Opened in August 2022 (June 2026 review). Selected for Tabelog Chinese TOKYO 100 in 2023, 2024 and 2026 (Tabelog). A June 2026 review describes it as Michelin-starred.
chef_bio.philosophy: Cantonese cooking honed over years, combined with seasonal Japanese ingredients, focusing on texture and aftertaste (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Shrimp with mango mayonnaise; seafood courses.

anecdotes.text: "By the way, the Chinese tea here rivals that of specialty tea shops, and it was the best I've had in a restaurant." — September 2026.
"The natural sweetness and fruity acidity of fresh mango shine through." — June 2026, shrimp with mango mayonnaise.
"I couldn't help but have high expectations after seeing the chef's background, but the result was just average, easy-to-eat Chinese food." — April 2025.

tokyo_saburoku_ningyocho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki layered with soba or udon noodles and a wheat batter, with sweet sauce; gansu is breaded fish cake.
tokyo_saburoku_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: okonomiyaki with pork, egg and squid tempura; the snacks are meat, offal and seafood.

Non-smoking. Opened 13 August 2020 (Tabelog).
tokyo_saburoku_ningyocho.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Ningyocho, Hiroshima okonomiyaki from a former Carp player] A small Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki counter run by Keisuke Yoshida, a 2002 draft pick of the Hiroshima Carp (June, July 2026 reviews), with baseball mascots by the door. The okonomiyaki is built on the griddle in front of you with soba or udon and a heap of green onion, using little flour and oil, so it eats lighter than it looks. Regulars, including Hiroshima natives, come for the local snacks too: gansu fish-cake fritters, kōne beef, salted horumon. The mood is relaxed and chatty, with high-school baseball on the TV (August 2026). Dishes are served on foil on the griddle and keep cooking, so eat promptly (March 2026). Book for weekend evenings.

roles: Owner ("Owned by former professional baseball player Keisuke Yoshida from the Hiroshima Carp", July 2026 review)
The master at the griddle ("Chef K", September 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Per 2026 reviews: owner Keisuke Yoshida was a second-round draft pick of the Hiroshima Carp in 2002 (June 2026); the shop opened on 13 August 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic (Tabelog; September 2026). "Located in Ningyocho, Saburoku is run by Keisuke Yoshida, who was drafted by the Carp in 2002." — June 2026.
"…they are served on aluminum foil on the teppan, so if you don’t eat quickly, they continue to cook" — March 2026.

tokyo_sushi_tsunoda_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an Edo-style fish sushi counter.

Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). 14 seats: 10 at a hinoki counter and two sunken-kotatsu private rooms for 2 and 4; private hire up to 20 (Tabelog; March 2026). Non-smoking. In business about 15 years (December 2025 review).
tokyo_sushi_tsunoda_ningyocho.notes: [Sushi · Ningyocho, a drinker's Edo-style counter with an ice-chilled fish box] A ten-seat hinoki sushi counter about fifteen years old (December 2025), whose fish rests in an old-style wooden refrigerator cooled with ice to keep it from drying. The chef is a drinker's chef: small rice, snacks between the nigiri, and plenty of sake (though no drinking while working, May 2022). The omakase is about ¥17,600 for a hairy-crab starter and fourteen pieces; highlights from recent diners include octopus that melts with the rice, flounder with its liver, and sea urchin served as nigiri. The chef is chatty and full of stories about curing and keeping fish (November 2025). Weekday lunch is by reservation, about ¥6,000. Closed weekends.

roles: Owner (unnamed; "The owner is friendly and fun", February 2025 review)
Head chef (unnamed; "The head chef is as lively as ever", September 2024 review)
chef_bio.background: In business about 15 years (December 2025 review). The chef explains traditional refrigeration and preservation methods, the ice-cooled wooden refrigerator and how fish is prepared (November, December 2025). Two staff at lunch (March 2025).

anecdotes.text: "While enjoying the recommended Japanese sake, I suggested, 'How about a drink for you too?' but … not to drink while working" — May 2022.
"I learned that the refrigerator uses ice to maintain a cool temperature, which helps keep the fish from drying out." — December 2025.
"I’ve never had octopus like this before, and I doubt I’ll find it again." — March 2026.

tokyo_renchin_taro_sweets_ningyocho.gf_detail: Ask. Cream puffs, roll cakes, egg tarts and baked taro cakes are wheat; taro paste, pudding and taro milk may not be, but nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_renchin_taro_sweets_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: milk drinks, egg tarts and cream puffs; zongzi with pork and egg yolk.

Operated by MARUFOODS (Tabelog remarks).
tokyo_renchin_taro_sweets_ningyocho.notes: [Sweets · Ningyocho, Taiwanese taro desserts from a century-old Keelung shop] A small takeaway counter on the ground floor of the KYOE PLAZA building on Amazake Yokocho, selling taro sweets from a Keelung shop with over a century of history; Japan has two branches, here and Takadanobaba (May 2026). The taro milk (¥680) is thick enough to drink as a paste, with tiny tapioca, and the taro puddings, roll cakes and black-rice taro squares are gently sweet. Everything is packed beautifully for gifts, and in early summer there are frozen Taiwanese zongzi. Prices have crept up (April 2026), and one May 2026 diner found the baked taro cake short on taro flavour. A couple of benches let you eat on the spot.

chef_bio.background: Per a May 2026 review: a branch of a long-established shop in Keelung, Taiwan, with over 100 years of history, with Japanese shops in Ningyocho and Takadanobaba. Opened 11 December 2021; operated by MARUFOODS (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The shop is a branch of a long-established store in Keelung, Taiwan, with over 100 years of history" — May 2026.
"The taro pudding features a delightful contrast between the smooth almond layer on top and the slightly grainy taro layer below" — September 2026.
"The price has been gradually increasing." — April 2026, on taro milk.

tokyo_sumibiyaki_18_shitaya.gf_detail: GF — ask: salt-grilled skewers are on the menu, but sauce-grilled skewers, kara-age, chicken nanban and the rice bowls are seasoned with unlisted sauces; nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_sumibiyaki_18_shitaya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a chicken restaurant — yakitori, oyakodon, kara-age, chicken nanban.
tokyo_sumibiyaki_18_shitaya.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 11:30–14:30 (last order 14:00) and 17:00–22:45 (last order 22:15); closed Mondays and the third Thursday of each month (Tabelog). Reservations taken, lunch included (December 2025); groups and bookings with children by phone. Appetizer charge ¥275 per person at night. 14 seats (counter 6, tables 9, plus 4 outside per Tabelog). Non-smoking (ashtrays outside). Cards, e-money and QR. Free Wi-Fi. Take-out. Opened 8 October 2022.
tokyo_sumibiyaki_18_shitaya.notes: [Yakitori · Uguisudani/Iriya, charcoal chicken and rice-bowl lunches] A small, clean charcoal-yakitori restaurant on the road between Uguisudani and Iriya, open since 2022, with a black-toned room of about six counter seats and a few tables. Lunch is the busy time: chicken rice bowls and set meals for about ¥1,000 — a yakitori bowl with four freshly grilled skewers, oyakodon with kara-age, chicken nanban — with miso soup and pickles, and it is open on Sundays, which is rare nearby. At night it is a yakitori izakaya with skewers from ¥242, a six-skewer omakase set and good sake; the white liver wins over even liver sceptics. Some 2026 lunch diners found portions small or the oyakodon chicken off; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog official listing. No source names the owner or cooks.

anecdotes.text: "The skewers were freshly grilled, crispy on the outside, and tender on the inside. It was delicious." — December 2025, yakitori rice bowl lunch.
"The biggest surprise was the white liver; I'm not usually a fan of liver, but it was so good that I wanted to order it again!" — October 2025.
"Unfortunately, the chicken in the Oyako-don had a slight odor, which was disappointing." — February 2026.

tokyo_alvino_ueno.gf_detail: GF — ask: the signature is a breaded croquette, and pasta, pizza and pâté en croûte are wheat; carpaccio, ajillo and salads are not described as gluten-free.
tokyo_alvino_ueno.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: Tabelog lists vegetarian options and there are vegetable pickles, olives, green salad and bagna cauda (with a creamy sauce), but nothing is marked vegan.
tokyo_alvino_ueno.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–4:00; Sun and holidays 17:00–23:30; closing days not fixed (Tabelog). Reservations taken; the sea-urchin croquette needs a reservation (Tabelog menu); seats may be limited to 2.5 hours when busy. Collect three reservation cards for a free bottle of wine (October 2026). 24 seats: counter on the ground floor, tables upstairs; the 2nd floor for groups of 8–20. Smoking allowed. Cards, e-money and QR. Take-away. Opened 26 July 2016.
tokyo_alvino_ueno.notes: [Italian bar · Ueno-Hirokoji, wine and sea-urchin croquettes until 4 am] A lively little Italian wine bar tucked into a back alley between Ueno and Yushima, open since 2016 and until 4 am except Sundays. Downstairs is a counter, upstairs tables for groups. The dish everyone orders is the sea-urchin cream croquette, stuffed with half an urchin (book ahead for it); then come crab-miso pasta, ajillo, seared wagyu carpaccio, pizza and generous appetizer plates, with a long wine list and quick, warm service that reviewers keep praising. Smoking is allowed inside. One September 2026 diner found it average for the price.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog remarks, the same operator runs AJILLO (Ueno, Nakano, Kanda Nishiguchi, Shimokitazawa), Bistronomie Avin, 角打ち割烹 CONBU, Gourmandise Alvino, Bar Buzz and Buzz Bee. No source names the chef.

anecdotes.text: "The classic sea urchin cream croquette was exquisite, but the real MVP this time was the ajillo!" — October 2026.
"Tucked away in a shady alley leading from Ueno to Nezu, this Italian restaurant is easy to miss on your first visit (laughs)." — October 2026.
"The quality and cost performance were average. Smoking is allowed here." — September 2026.

tokyo_prost_tokyo_ueno.gf_detail: GF — ask: the house sausages are described as additive-free fresh meat, but casings, fillers and sauces are not described, and pasta, bread and desserts are on the menu; nothing is labelled gluten-free.
tokyo_prost_tokyo_ueno.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: Tabelog lists vegetarian options, and vegetables come from the restaurant's own farm (bagna cauda, salads), but most dishes are sausage, smoked meat, fish and cheese; nothing is marked vegan.
tokyo_prost_tokyo_ueno.hours_raw: Mon–Fri and the day before a holiday 17:00–23:00; Sat, Sun and holidays 16:00–23:00; last order food 22:00, drinks 22:30; closing time may vary; closing days not fixed (Tabelog). Reservations by phone 16:00–23:00 or online any time; same-day cancellations charged. If full, the sister shop Prost Tokyo Akihabara (7–10 min walk) serves the same menu. Table charge ¥770 per person (not on courses); private rooms add 10%. 50 seats; private rooms for 2–8. Non-smoking. Cards and QR (PayPay, Rakuten Pay); no e-money. Children welcome. BYO allowed. Opened 15 November 2016.
tokyo_prost_tokyo_ueno.notes: [Sausage & smoke bar · Ueno-Hirokoji, house sausages from around the world] A dim, wood-toned sixth-floor bar a minute from Ueno-Hirokoji Station, open since 2016, that makes its own additive-free sausages — around twenty kinds through the year, from German Thüringer and weisswurst to a habanero Spanish sausage and a shiso one — and smokes salmon, duck, pancetta, cheese and even drinks in-house. Vegetables come from its own farm in Ibaraki, best in the raclette grill. Expect about ¥4,000–5,000 a head with a ¥770 table charge (none on courses); there are private rooms for couples and small groups. Most 2026 reviewers enjoyed the sausages and smoked plates; one in October 2026 found the food and drinks unremarkable. If it is full, the Akihabara branch has the same menu.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog official listing; sister shop Prost Tokyo Akihabara. The menu describes in-house sausage making (stuffing, drying, smoking) and a farm, Prost Farm, in Ibaraki Prefecture. No source names the operator or cooks.
chef_bio.philosophy: Additive-free sausages with no chemical seasonings or preservatives (Tabelog menu).

anecdotes.text: "From a selection of over a dozen types of sausages, I chose two: the Spanish habanero and garlic sausage, and the French tapenade with olives and anchovies sausage." — September 2026.
"The smoked umeshu has a rich aroma, and when you taste it, the fruity flavor bursts forth with minimal bitterness" — October 2026.
"The food isn't bad, but it's not particularly delicious either, and I wasn't impressed." — October 2026.

tokyo_raffles_curry_taito.hours_raw: Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri 11:45–16:00 and 18:00–21:30; Tue 11:45–14:00 and 18:00–21:30; Sat 11:45–16:00; closed Sundays and holidays (Tabelog; may change). A November 2026 diner found it shut during posted hours on a weekday of a long holiday, with no notice on social media and no answer by phone. No reservations; a short queue at weekday noon (October 2026). Cash only. 7 counter seats. Non-smoking. Take-out.
tokyo_raffles_curry_taito.notes: [Curry · Naka-Okachimachi, a seven-seat counter of gentle curries] A tiny counter curry shop, marked only by a sign, a few minutes from Naka-Okachimachi Station and a regular on Tabelog's Tokyo curry 100 lists. The curries are smooth and mild rather than fiery — chicken curry (¥950) heaped with tender chicken, a vegetable keema full of green beans and daikon, a deeper mutton — and most people get two in one plate for about ¥1,500. Seven seats fill fast at lunch; it is open in the evening on weekdays, cash only, closed Sundays and holidays. Reviewers who want heat find it too gentle even at the top spice level, one October 2026 diner thought the kitchen a bit dirty, and one in November 2026 found it closed without notice during posted hours.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog listing (Curry TOKYO 100: 2023, 2024, 2026). No source names the owner or cook.

anecdotes.text: "Both were the type of curry I love—smooth and not overly spicy, with a mild salty flavor." — October 2026, chicken curry and vegetable keema.
"The tender chicken was indeed plentiful, just as the reviews said, making it very satisfying to eat." — October 2026, chicken curry ¥950.
"However, even after the opening time, there was no sign of it being open, and I couldn't get through on the phone." — November 2026.

tokyo_niku_kaiseki_rinzen_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the shop asks guests to tell it about allergies or dietary restrictions in advance (Tabelog). Courses include a Chateaubriand katsu sandwich, sukiyaki and soy-based sauces, so wheat is in several dishes.
tokyo_niku_kaiseki_rinzen_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a beef kaiseki with dashi-based dishes and seafood.
tokyo_niku_kaiseki_rinzen_yotsuya.hours_raw: Daily lunch 12:00–14:30 (last order 13:30) and dinner 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:30) (Tabelog). Reservation only; allergies and dietary needs in advance; children only if in the upper years of elementary school order the course (Tabelog). Service charge 10% (Tabelog). 14 seats: a private counter for 4 with an open kitchen and table rooms; private rooms for 2–8; hire up to 20; non-smoking (Tabelog; October 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). The à la carte menu offered at opening has been dropped (September 2026).
tokyo_niku_kaiseki_rinzen_yotsuya.notes: [Kaiseki · Yotsuya, wagyu kaiseki with a generous free-flow] A dark, modern Japanese room on Shinjuku-dōri where premium wagyu is cooked kaiseki-style, course by course, in front of a four-seat private counter or in table rooms. The Omakase Rinzen course (¥19,800, or ¥22,000 with two hours of drinks) opens with beef yukhoe under Kaluga caviar and runs through a Chateaubriand katsu sandwich, charcoal-grilled beef with fresh wasabi and sukiyaki to matsutake rice in autumn; what regulars rave about is the free-flow list, with champagne, premium sake and Yamazaki and Hakushu whisky. One regular counts a dozen visits. Not every visit pleased: a September 2026 lunch diner found the ¥7,000 course small, especially the rice, and headed the review "a restaurant catering to foreign tourists"; another missed the old à la carte menu. Reservation only; 10% service.

chef_bio.background: No source names the chef or owner. Tabelog: Japanese cuisine of Kobe beef and "Ota beef" heifers (as machine-translated), seasonal seafood and mountain produce, gratitude to producers across Japan; concept "providing customers with a memorable experience". 2026 reviewers describe the beef as Tajima beef and note the chef cooking at the private counter.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Providing customers with a memorable experience" (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Wagyu caviar yukhoe; Chateaubriand katsu sandwich; free-flow drinks.

anecdotes.text: "I can't even count how many times I've visited this beloved restaurant… we enjoyed a seasonal course priced at JPY 22,000, featuring plenty of matsutake mushrooms." — September 2026, a 12th visit.
"Whiskey lovers will appreciate that Yamazaki, Hakushu, and Hibiki are included in the all-you-can-drink selection." — September 2026.
"A restaurant catering to foreign tourists… I was surprised by how little there was, especially the rice." — September 2026, ¥7,000 lunch course.

tokyo_sushi_hide_sono_ni_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. Sushi is seasoned at the counter and the omakase includes cooked appetizers; the staff checked a companion's allergies on one October 2025 visit, but nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_sushi_hide_sono_ni_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish and shellfish omakase, including whale on some days.
tokyo_sushi_hide_sono_ni_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri lunch 11:30–13:30 and dinner 17:30–22:30; Sat dinner only; closed Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). Reservations taken; lunch can end early when the sushi rice runs out, so call first (May 2024). Dinner is one of two omakase courses (Tabelog). 15 seats: a counter, a 4-person private room, tatami and sunken seating; hire up to 20; non-smoking (Tabelog; March 2024). Cards and PayPay or Rakuten Pay; no e-money (Tabelog). Renewed in November 2018 after 23 years as Sushi Hide (Tabelog).
tokyo_sushi_hide_sono_ni_yotsuya.notes: [Sushi · Yotsuya, a renewed neighbourhood sushi counter] On a Sanei-cho street with several sushi shops, a calm, clean counter that served Yotsuya for 23 years as Sushi Hide and reopened, renewed, as "Sono Ni" (number two) in November 2018. The omakase leans on small dishes — house shiokara, steamed abalone with whale bacon, Shimane horse mackerel, young ayu in spring — before a modest run of nigiri, with plenty of sake and some wines to match; one diner calls it perfect for drink lovers, another wished for more nigiri. Lunch is a ¥3,500 chirashi or nigiri set, best at the counter. A quiet, watchful head chef and several apprentices; regulars can make the counter lively. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.origin: Sushi Hide for 23 years in Yotsuya, renewed as すし秀 其ノ弐 in November 2018 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.background: No source names the chef. Tabelog (corporate-member listing): "After 23 years of satisfying food lovers in Yotsuya, we renewed our restaurant in November 2018… Sushi Hideo No. 2" (machine-translated); dinner is only two omakase courses. Reviews describe a quiet head chef who picked up on a diner's dislikes and offered alternatives (August 2023), "the number of apprentices" (October 2025), and a scene of the TV drama Ousama ni Sasagu Kusuriyubi shot at the shop late at night (May 2024).

anecdotes.text: "When seated at a table, the sushi is served on a plate, while at the counter, each piece is hand-crafted upon order, making the counter experience feel more worthwhile!" — May 2024, ¥3,500 nigiri lunch.
"A sushi restaurant with plenty of appetizers and fewer nigiri, perfect for drink lovers… The homemade shio-kara is truly delicious." — May 2025.
"Steamed abalone with whale bacon… Donchicchi horse mackerel from Shimane Prefecture." — July 2026, omakase.

Cash only (Tabelog). 8 seats at a U-shaped counter; non-smoking (Tabelog; September 2026).
tokyo_horai_wakaba_yotsuya.notes: [Chinese · Yotsuya, a family-run lunch counter near Suga Shrine] An eight-seat U-shaped counter in a quiet residential pocket near Suga Shrine, open just two and a half hours on four weekdays and still packed, with construction workers and office regulars lining up outside. Order by voice: a "special" ramen gets a spoonful of back fat that sweetens and enriches the soy broth, with wontons, chashu or spicy takana on top, and almost everyone adds a jumbo shumai at ¥100, if it hasn't sold out. A ¥200 wonton soup and a moist five-ingredient fried rice are the other quiet stars. Most bowls cost about ¥1,000. Regulars chat with the owner at the counter. Cash only.

roles: Family-run (August 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: No source names the owner. "Considering it was during the Obon holiday and it's a family-run place, there was a high chance they might be closed" (August 2026); "listening to the conversations between the local regulars and the owner" (April 2026).

anecdotes.text: "The difference between the regular wonton noodle soup and the special version is not in the ingredients, but in the broth—one has back fat while the other does not." — August 2026.

"Special Chashu Wonton Ramen JPY 1150, Jumbo Shumai (1 piece) JPY 100… by after 12, it was fully packed and there was a line outside." — May 2026.

tokyo_yakiniku_666_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. Salted tongue and plain grilled cuts can be eaten with salt, but the tare, sukiyaki-style dishes, cold noodles and bibimbap are wheat- or soy-based; nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_yakiniku_666_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a wagyu yakiniku; kimchi and salads are the only plant sides named.
tokyo_yakiniku_666_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–14:30 and 17:00–23:30; Sat, Sun and holidays 11:00–14:30 and 17:00–23:00; closing days not fixed (Tabelog). Reservations taken. Service charge 10% (Tabelog). 28 seats: a counter of 4, four private rooms and one room for 8; strollers only in the room for 8; hire up to 20 (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Paid parking behind the shop (Tabelog).
tokyo_yakiniku_666_yotsuya.notes: [Yakiniku · Yotsuya, lean rare wagyu in private rooms] A calm, concrete-and-wood yakiniku by a golden cow on Shinjuku-dōri — the name, one diner learned, is read "Mutsumi" — specialising in lean, chewy wagyu from small farms: about 90 head a year of Mikumanogyu and 7 of the rarer Mansukagyu. Most tables are private rooms, and the courses run from 19 to 25 small dishes, from rare thick tongue and seared yukhoe with uni and ikura to a six-cut platter and a sirloin mille-feuille, with cold noodles to finish. Diners agree on the quality of the meat; several 2026 visitors found the courses small for the price and the drinks dear, one found the service slow and the bill shown openly, another missed any greeting or explanation, and one found an overseas staff member's Japanese hard to follow but praised the effort. 10% service.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner. Tabelog (corporate-member listing): carefully selected wagyu, "90 head of 'Mikumanogyu' and 7 head of 'Mansukagyu' each year"; a lineup of lean cuts from farmers who prioritise taste, with less marbling for a more satisfying chew. An August 2026 diner: "The name is read as 'Mutsumi.'"
chef_bio.philosophy: Adult yakiniku: high-quality meat and good sake in a calm space (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "Dining at 'Yakiniku 666' in Yotsuya. The name is read as 'Mutsumi.' It's about a 5-minute walk from Yotsuya Sanchome Station, marked by a golden cow statue." — August 2026.
"Overall, I have no complaints about the quality of the meat. However, the portion size of the course is quite small for the price." — May 2026, Shinra Bansho course.
"The loin melts in your mouth, while the short ribs have just the right amount of chewiness without being overly fatty—simply exquisite." — July 2026.

tokyo_kanimura_ueno.gf_detail: GF — ask: Tabelog's checklist marks gluten-free options, but no dish is named; the buffet mixes sushi with soy sauce, Chinese dishes, tempura, curry and desserts.
tokyo_kanimura_ueno.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: Tabelog's checklist marks vegan and vegetarian options, but no dish is named; the buffet is built around crab, seafood, sushi and meat.
tokyo_kanimura_ueno.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–22:00, last entry 20:00; open all year; buffet at lunch too (Tabelog). Reservations taken; fully private rooms with doors carry a ¥3,000 room fee. Buffet runs 120 minutes. Children 4–12 half price, under 4 free. 160 seats; private rooms for 2 to 30+. Non-smoking (smoking area outside). Cards and QR (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay); no e-money. Menus in English, Chinese and Korean; staff speak English, Chinese and Korean. Wheelchair accessible; free Wi-Fi. Opened 5 March 2025; renovated by October 2026.
tokyo_kanimura_ueno.notes: [Seafood buffet · Okachimachi, all-you-can-eat crab by the station] A big, bright crab-and-seafood buffet a minute from Okachimachi Station, opened in 2025 by the group behind Ginza's 銀座八芳 seafood buffet. After a renovation it became a self-service spread: boiled snow crab and king crab to grill at your table, shellfish from the tank, sashimi and Edo-style sushi, wagyu that staff grill for you at a central counter, Chinese dishes such as Peking duck, and desserts down to Häagen-Dazs. It costs ¥9,800 for 120 minutes with drinks (¥8,820 on promotion in October 2026), more for a king-crab course; children are half price. Private rooms with doors suit groups. Reviewers in 2026 were mostly thrilled with the crab; one asked for a cheaper price for non-drinkers.

chef_bio.background: Run by FANG DREAM COMPANY, whose brands include 銀座八芳, 銀座七芳, 銀座芳亭, 孫二娘 and 魚でん (Compalyze, August 2026); OZmall (May 2025) calls it a 系列店 of 銀座八芳. A second かに村, the 銀座新橋店, is listed on Gnavi. No source names the cooks.

anecdotes.text: "The biggest change is that the previous table-ordering buffet style has been replaced with a self-service buffet" — October 2026, ¥9,800 for 120 minutes, ¥8,820 on promotion.

tokyo_edo_tempura_yonmonsen_ueno.notes: [Tempura · Okachimachi, Edo-style tempura bar by the station] A small, casual sake bar a minute from Okachimachi Station that fries tempura to order by the piece — vegetables from ¥90, shrimp ¥400, a seafood plate ¥980 — and finishes with 100% buckwheat soba. Around it are sashimi, kombu-cured sea bream, eel and grilled eel-liver skewers, with sake. It reopened in February 2026 after a renovation, now with QR ordering and cashless payment; some old favourites like curry soba and whale sashimi have gone. No appetizer charge, and evenings are often full, so book. Closed Wednesdays.

tokyo_craft_burger_jiro_matsugaya.notes: [Burgers · Kappabashi, a dog-friendly craft burger bar] A small burger shop on Kappabashi Hon-dōri, a short walk from the kitchenware street, open since 2019 and happy to seat your dog — there is even roast beef on a dog menu. The burgers are thick 100% beef patties on a menu of about fifteen, from a ¥1,200 hamburger to the green-onion Edo Senju negi burger and the stacked greedy burger, each with fries and a mini salad; add a drink at lunch for ¥150. In the evening one frequent visitor treats it as a bar, with craft beer, fish and chips and grilled chashu. Reviewers find the prices fair for craft burgers. It is about ten minutes from the nearest stations; closed Mondays.

tokyo_kakuuchi_kappo_conbu_yushima.notes: [Sake bar · Yushima, retro standing-bar kappō until 3 am] A tiny, retro sake bar in a quiet Yushima alley, opened in December 2025 by the team behind the Italian bar Alvino, pairing kappō-style dishes with a weekly-changing list of 10–15 sakes. Sit at the six-seat counter or stand outside with a glass. The dish everyone talks about is the dote-ni, pork simmered in a special miso until it rivals braised pork; seafood yukhoe, miso cream udon and a shellfish rice soup are close behind, served on Arita and Kutani ware. Staff explain the sakes well. It is small and popular, so book; at busy times food and drinks can be slow. Smoking is allowed, ¥500 cover; open to 3 am except Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog remarks, run by the group behind Alvino and AJILLO; two staff run the room (October 2026). No source names the cooks.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per a September 2026 review, the concept is "sake calls for side dishes, and people call for flavor."

anecdotes.text: "The Dote-ni, in particular, was the best I've ever had at an izakaya." — October 2026.
"The staff were also very attentive and provided thorough explanations." — September 2026, sake.
"However, because of its popularity, it takes some time for the drinks and food to be served, so it's important to order early at this izakaya." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (公式情報): 角打ち割烹 CONBU、文京区湯島3-43-11 阿部ビル 1F、湯島駅、上野広小路・上野御徒町・仲御徒町駅A3出口から徒歩3分、火〜土・祝・祝前日・祝後日17:00〜翌3:00 (料理L.O.2:00、ドリンクL.O.2:30)、日17:00〜23:00、月曜休み、予約可、お通し500円、16席 (カウンター6、2人テーブル2、外の立ち飲み6)、喫煙可、カード・電子マネー・QR可、2025年12月12日オープン、Alvino、AJILLO などの系列。メニュー (2025年12月): 生ガキと海苔の春巻き700円、ズワイガニのカニ味噌クリームコロッケ650円、大和芋のとろろ鍋1,300円、おばんざい3種600円、白レバーの梅酒煮900円。口コミ (2026年8〜10月): 名物の土手煮、海鮮ユッケ、貝の雑炊、味噌クリームうどん、毎週替わる10〜15種の日本酒、有田焼と九谷焼の器、予約が取りにくい、スタッフ2人、混むと提供に時間がかかる。

tokyo_ikoma_ken_ningyocho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles, gyoza and soy-based ankake sauces.
tokyo_ikoma_ken_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: town-Chinese dishes with pork, shrimp and squid.
tokyo_ikoma_ken_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 12:00–15:00 and 18:30–21:00; Sat 11:00–14:00; closed Sunday (Tabelog). Diners mention it being closed when they tried at lunch (September 2026) and full in the evening (August 2026). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Cash only — no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). 20 seats; smoking allowed (Tabelog). One cook at times, so waits of about 20 minutes (September 2026).
tokyo_ikoma_ken_ningyocho.notes: [Chinese · Ningyocho, a decades-old town-Chinese counter with unchanged prices] A classic machi-chuka on Amazake Yokocho, dating from the Taisho era by one account and the Showa era by another (2026 reviews). It is one of several Tokyo shops sharing the Ikoma-ken name through the old noren-wake system rather than a chain, and a September 2026 diner calls it the oldest still open. The draws are hearty Cantonese noodles loaded with seafood and vegetables (¥800), crisp gyoza (¥550) and ramen at ¥550, at prices one diner found unchanged in six years. Pickled plums sit on the table to reset the palate. Lunch fills with locals; at busy times one cook handles everything, so expect a wait. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Per 2026 reviews: established in the Taisho era (July 2026) or around since the Showa era (May 2026); the Ikoma-ken name spread through a traditional noren-wake franchise system, mainly in Tokyo, and the Ningyocho shop seems to be the oldest remaining (September 2026). A diner came after seeing it introduced by Nayumi Shiomi (September 2026).

anecdotes.text: "Ikoma Ken is a restaurant that has spread not as a chain but through a traditional franchise system, primarily in Tokyo." — September 2026.
"I can't believe there are still places like this nowadays." — August 2026, on prices unchanged in six years.
"Interestingly, the sugar container had pickled plums inside. According to the staff, it's meant to cleanse the palate." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 生駒軒、中華料理、ラーメン、日本橋人形町2-3-4、月〜金12:00〜15:00、18:30〜21:00、土11:00〜14:00、日曜休み、予約可、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、20席、喫煙可。口コミ(2026年5月〜10月): 町中華、大正創業という声と昭和からという声、のれん分けの生駒軒で人形町が現存最古らしい、ラーメン550円、定食800円、広東麺800円、五目あんかけ800円、タンメン700円、チャーハン800円、餃子550円、6年間値上げなし、卓上に梅干し、昼は混む、厨房がひとりのときは待つ。

cultural_comfort.note: A busy local Chinese diner; cash only; smoking allowed.
