tokyo_kaimen_fukagawa_ningyocho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles (Hokkaido Yumechikara wheat, October 2026).
tokyo_kaimen_fukagawa_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: clam broth blended with a beef-bone white broth, topped with pork and chicken chashu.
tokyo_kaimen_fukagawa_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–14:30 and 16:00–23:00; Sun 11:00–14:30 and 16:00–20:00; closed holidays (Tabelog). Ticket machine; buy first (October 2026). No reservations. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB), e-money and PayPay (Tabelog). 8 counter seats (Tabelog). Queues at weekday noon and weekend lunch, about 10 people one rainy Saturday (October 2026). Opened 23 December 2025 (Tabelog).
tokyo_kaimen_fukagawa_ningyocho.notes: [Ramen · Ningyocho, clam-broth ramen on Amazake Yokocho] A small eight-seat ramen counter opened in December 2025, run by an owner who learned ramen at Shichiri in Ogikubo and is supervised by Kaimen Mikawa in Shimokitazawa (Tabelog). The broth is all clams, asari among them, rounded out with a little beef-bone white broth, rich but clean, and the bowl carries three kinds of chashu. Shoyu and shio are the classics; there is also miso with thick noodles and a shellfish mazesoba, plus a small asari rice. Diners rave about the broth, though one found the chashu a poor match for it and another the room noisy, with loud patrons left unchecked (October 2026). Expect a short queue at lunch.

roles: Owner (unnamed; trained at Shichiri, Ogikubo; supervised by Kaimen Mikawa, Shimokitazawa — Tabelog remarks)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: opened 23 December 2025; the owner learned ramen at Shichiri in Ogikubo and received supervision from Kaimen Mikawa in Shimokitazawa, with a strong commitment to shellfish noodles. Per an October 2026 review: broth of asari and other clams blended with a beef-bone half-white broth; noodles of Hokkaido Yumechikara wheat.

anecdotes.text: "According to the description, … also use beef bone broth, which enhances the clam flavor while adding a deep richness." — May 2026.
"My first impression was that it tasted like clam miso soup!" — October 2026, miso ramen.
"…three types of chashu … which are decent on their own but don’t quite match the clam broth." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 貝麺ふか川、ラーメン、日本橋人形町2-3-4、月〜土11:00〜14:30、16:00〜23:00、日11:00〜14:30、16:00〜20:00、祝日休み、予約不可、カード・電子マネー・PayPay可、8席、2025年12月23日オープン、店主はOgikubo の Shichiri でラーメンを学び、Shimokitazawa の Kaimen Mikawa の監修。口コミ(2026年5月〜10月): あさりなどの貝の白湯に牛骨の半白湯、3種のチャーシュー、醤油と塩、味噌は太麺、まぜそば、あさりご飯、Hokkaido の Yumechikara の麺、券売機、昼は行列、チャーシューがスープに合わない・騒がしい客を注意しないという声も。

tokyo_iwateya_ningyocho.gf_detail: Ask. Oden broth is soy-based, and many oden items (chikuwa-bu, fish cakes) contain wheat; sashimi with soy sauce (2023–25 reviews). Nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_iwateya_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: oden in a dashi broth, sashimi and yakitori.
tokyo_iwateya_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 17:00–22:00; closed Sat, Sun and holidays (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; fills early with regulars (September 2025). Cash only (July 2024; Tabelog). No prices on the menu, but bills are reasonable (2023–25 reviews). 11 seats at an L-shaped counter (Tabelog; December 2023). Smoking allowed (Tabelog). Popular items such as natto-stuffed grilled tofu sell out by later in the evening (February 2025). Featured on "Onna Sakaba Hourouki", broadcast 9 August 2019 (Tabelog), and on "Sakaba Hourouki" (May 2025 review).
tokyo_iwateya_ningyocho.notes: [Oden · Ningyocho, a Showa izakaya kept by the founder's granddaughter] An eleven-seat L-shaped counter that has served oden and sashimi for over sixty years, founded by someone from Iwate and now run by the third-generation proprietress, the founder's granddaughter (December 2023, May 2025). The proprietress runs the room alone, with the proprietress's husband doing the buying and prep (September 2025). Oden simmers in front of the counter; the sashimi list runs to about fourteen kinds, and there's hot sake and Iwate sake to go with it. There are no prices on the menu, but bills come in modest. Regulars pack it early, yet first-timers are welcomed warmly. It has appeared on Sakaba Hourouki and Onna Sakaba Hourouki. Cash only; weekdays only.

roles: Third-generation proprietress, the founder's granddaughter (December 2023, May 2025 reviews)
The proprietress's husband handles sourcing and preparation (September 2025 review)
chef_bio.origin: The founder came from Iwate Prefecture, hence the name (December 2023, May 2025 reviews)
chef_bio.background: Per reviews: established over 60 years ago by a founder from Iwate; now run by the third-generation proprietress, the founder's granddaughter (December 2023, May 2025). The counter resembles that of a former sushi shop (September 2025). Featured in "Sakaba Hourouki" and "Onna Sakaba Hourouki" (Tabelog; May 2025).

anecdotes.text: "As the name suggests, it was opened by the first generation from Iwate, and now the third-generation granddaughter manages the establishment." — May 2025.
"The restaurant is run by a mother who manages everything" — September 2025.
"I was worried about the prices since they weren't listed anywhere, but despite having a decent amount to drink, the prices were very reasonable." — September 2025.

tokyo_kushiage_nakaya_ningyocho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: every skewer is in a wheat batter and breadcrumbs, and dessert is fried bread.
tokyo_kushiage_nakaya_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: meat and seafood skewers.
tokyo_kushiage_nakaya_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:30–22:30 (last order 22:00); Sun 17:00–21:30 (last order 21:00); closing days irregular (Tabelog). Reservations from 17:30 to 22:00 (Sun 17:00–21:00); tell the shop about allergies and dislikes when booking (Tabelog). Cards, transport IC, Edy, iD, QUICPay, PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay, au PAY, Alipay and WeChat Pay (Tabelog). 20 seats including a counter and a private room for 5–6; private rooms for 3 or more can be booked at the sister shop in Kodenmacho (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Ordering by mobile phone (July 2026). Opened 27 May 2017 (Tabelog).
tokyo_kushiage_nakaya_ningyocho.notes: [Kushiage · Ningyocho, an omakase kushiage counter in an old-house room] A second-floor kushiage room near the Amazake Yokocho crossing, the sister of Yanagibashi's Kushiemon, which has fried Edo-style skewers for over forty years (Tabelog). Skewers come one by one in a very thin, crisp batter, each matched to one of ten house sauces, from shiso-wrapped shrimp to wagyu with zucchini, until you say stop; finish with fried bread dusted with cocoa or kinako. Sake and wine are chosen to match. Diners like the calm, old-house feel and the light frying, but ordering is by phone only (July 2026), service can be stretched (October 2026), and one August 2026 party of three found the omakase bill (¥36,000) higher than expected — set a budget.

chef_bio.background: Opened 27 May 2017 (Tabelog). Per Tabelog: a sister restaurant of Yanagibashi Kushiemon, serving Edo-style kushiage for over 40 years; a sister shop, Kushiage Nakaya Kodenmacho, takes private-room bookings for three or more. An October 2026 reviewer notes the menu and ten sauces match Kushiemon's.
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal ingredients in an ultra-thin, crispy batter with ten sauces (Tabelog shop text).

anecdotes.text: "The kushiage here features a light batter, making every skewer delicious." — June 2026.
"However, it was disappointing that the menu was only available through mobile ordering." — July 2026.
"The skewers were delicious, but I was surprised by the final bill—it was too high. We spent JPY 36000 for three people." — August 2026.

tokyo_guruatsu_stand_matsugaya.gf_detail: GF — ask: a May 2017 review called it a gluten-free scone and muffin shop, but a November 2018 review says the tofu muffins use whole-wheat flour; check each item.
tokyo_guruatsu_stand_matsugaya.vegan_detail: Some vegan options: per 2018 reviews, the muffins and scones are made without butter, eggs, milk, white sugar or oil, using organic soy milk and tofu, and the lunch deli is vegetable-only (2021); a 2017 reviewer was unsure whether everything is strictly vegan, so ask.
tokyo_guruatsu_stand_matsugaya.hours_raw: Wednesdays and Fridays 11:30–16:00; closed other days (Tabelog; may change). Take-out only; no reservations. Cash only (no cards, e-money or QR, per Tabelog). Popular items such as zunda sweets can sell out by noon (November 2021). Online shop on BASE.
tokyo_guruatsu_stand_matsugaya.notes: [Bakery & deli · Kappabashi, plant-based muffins to take away] A tiny take-out stand on the back streets behind Kappabashi, open only on Wednesdays and Fridays, selling palm-sized muffins and scones made with tofu and soy milk rather than butter, eggs or milk, plus a vegetable-only lunch box (¥880 in 2020) and natural foods. The muffins are chewy, almost mochi-like, and only lightly sweet; flavours change, from chocolate banana and matcha-chestnut to beet and white chocolate. Most reviews are from 2017–2021, with a July 2026 visitor still buying soy-milk muffins. Cash only; the popular flavours go early.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog listing; a 2018 review mentions a second Guruatsu with eat-in seating closer to Ueno, and a 2017 review says the shop sells at the Aoyama Farmers Market. No source names the owner.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per 2018 reviews: baking without butter, margarine, eggs, milk, white sugar or preservatives.
chef_bio.specialty: Tofu and soy-milk muffins and scones.

anecdotes.text: "This place offers incredibly healthy bread made without butter, margarine, eggs, milk, white sugar, or preservatives." — November 2018.
"This Zunda muffin has a pleasantly chewy texture from the soymilk and a perfect level of sweetness." — July 2020, soy-milk zunda muffin (limited).
"I took home three muffins to enjoy." — July 2026, soy-milk muffins.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: Guruatsu STAND、松が谷3-8-4、稲荷町駅から徒歩10分、JR上野駅から15分、水・金11:30〜16:00、ほかは休み、テイクアウトのみ、予約不可、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、野菜にこだわり、ベジタリアン向け。口コミ (2017年5月〜2026年7月): 豆腐と豆乳のマフィンとスコーン、チョコバナナマフィン340円、抹茶と栗、ビーツとホワイトチョコの豆腐マフィン、豆乳ずんだ、塩バナナスコーン、オーガニック野菜の野菜ボックス880円、バター・マーガリン・卵・牛乳・白砂糖・保存料不使用 (2018年)、全粒粉 (2018年)、2017年にはグルテンフリーのスコーンとマフィンの店という声、もちもちの食感、人気の品は昼に売り切れ、上野寄りにイートインのある店も、青山ファーマーズマーケットにも出店。

cultural_comfort.note: Take-out counter; point at the muffins; cash only.

tokyo_craft_ramen_bit_shitaya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: consommé broths with pork chashu, and a venison broth and venison chashu in the premium bowl.
tokyo_craft_ramen_bit_shitaya.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 11:00–14:30 (last order 14:15) and 17:30–20:00 (last order 19:45); closed Wednesdays and some other days, announced monthly on social media (Tabelog). No reservations. Tickets from a machine. Cash only (no cards, e-money or QR). 7 counter seats. Non-smoking. Opened 26 February 2024.
tokyo_craft_ramen_bit_shitaya.notes: [Ramen · Iriya, consommé ramen at a café-like counter] A seven-seat ramen counter in an alley near Iriya Station, opened in 2024 by a chef from the well-known Ramen Kai, that looks more like a calm café than a ramen shop. The broths are consommés, clear and deep: a shio and a shoyu with fine thin noodles and tender chashu (about ¥1,250 with egg), a ¥1,700 premium shio, and a limited Takumi bowl built on venison with a steak-like venison chashu (¥2,350). Reviewers in 2026 call it craft ramen in every sense; one questioned the ¥2,000-plus price of the consommé bowl. Cash only; closed Wednesdays, and evening hours are short.

chef_bio.background: Per an October 2026 review, run by a chef from the renowned Ramen Kai, specialising in consommé-based ramen. No source names the chef.

anecdotes.text: "The broth, made with venison, features venison chashu that resembles a steak rather than traditional chashu." — October 2026, Takumi consommé ramen ¥2,350.
"The beautifully presented bowl immediately catches the eye with its clear broth." — October 2026, shoyu ramen.
"But I wonder what the deal is with the consomme ramen that costs over JPY 2000?" — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (公式情報): Craft Ramen BiT、下谷1-12-25 1F、入谷駅から徒歩3分、JR鶯谷駅南口から7分、JR上野駅入谷口から10分、月火木金土日11:00〜14:30 (L.O.14:15)・17:30〜20:00 (L.O.19:45)、水曜休み (ほか不定休、SNSで告知)、予約不可、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、カウンター7席、禁煙、2024年2月26日オープン。口コミ (2024年7月〜2026年10月): 有名店のRamen Kai出身の店主によるコンソメのラーメン、塩と醤油、細麺、澄んだスープ、味玉醤油ラーメン1,250円、特製塩ラーメン1,700円、限定の「匠」は鹿のスープと鹿のチャーシュー、味玉付き2,350円、替え玉300円、カフェのような落ち着いた店内、コンソメのラーメンの値段に疑問の声も。

tokyo_ramen_nagayama_negishi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles (thin or thick) in a chicken and pork-bone broth.

One person ran the shop on an October 2026 evening. Opened 15 December 2007.
tokyo_ramen_nagayama_negishi.notes: [Ramen · Uguisudani, rich chicken-and-pork ramen since 2007] A small L-shaped ramen counter just across the overpass from Uguisudani's South Exit, open since 2007 and still one of the area's most popular bowls. The broth is a thick, creamy blend of chicken paitan and pork bone that clings to the noodles yet is not too salty, served as shoyu, miso or tsukemen, with tender chashu; you choose thick or thin noodles, and a large portion (up to 400 g for tsukemen) costs nothing extra. Ramen is about ¥950, a seasoned-egg chashu bowl ¥1,350. Open until nearly midnight except Sundays; closed Mondays. Cash only, and smoking is allowed except at lunch.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog listing. An October 2026 diner saw one person running the shop. No source names the owner.

anecdotes.text: "The rich and impactful broth was a delightful blend of chicken and pork bone flavors." — September 2026, ramen ¥950.
"You can increase the portion for free up to 400 grams, so of course, I went for the maximum." — September 2026, tsukemen.
"The noodles were flat and on the softer side. The broth was average." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: ラーメン長山、根岸1-3-21、JR鶯谷駅南口から徒歩3分、火〜土11:00〜23:50、日11:00〜22:00、月曜休み、予約不可、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、カウンター12席、喫煙可 (12:00〜13:00は禁煙)、2007年12月15日オープン。口コミ (2026年9〜11月): 鶏白湯と豚骨の濃厚でクリーミーなスープ、ラーメン950円、味玉チャーシュー麺1,350円、味噌、醤油、つけ麺、大盛り無料 (つけ麺は400gまで)、太麺か細麺、卓上に七味、こしょう、辛味噌、にんにく、豆板醤、夜は一人で切り盛り、スープは普通という声も。

cultural_comfort.note: Ticket machine; staff ask size and noodle thickness; cash only.

tokyo_junshukou_gin_yushima.gf_detail: GF — ask: sashimi-led seafood menu, but simmered fish, tempura and hot pots are seasoned with unlisted sauces; nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_junshukou_gin_yushima.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish izakaya — sashimi, simmered fish, kue hot pot on bonito dashi, crab, oysters.
tokyo_junshukou_gin_yushima.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–22:00; closed Sundays, holidays, Obon, New Year and some other days (Tabelog). Reservations taken (easy to book, March 2026); children by phone. 16 seats: about 6 at the counter and 3 tables (September 2026). Heated-tobacco smoking area. Tabelog lists cards and QR (PayPay, au PAY); a September 2026 diner was charged a 3% surcharge for non-cash payment.
tokyo_junshukou_gin_yushima.notes: [Izakaya · Yushima, a hidden second-floor fish and sake bar] A small, quiet izakaya up the stairs of a Yushima building, easy to miss from the street, where the master is from Saitama and the counter seats face the kitchen. Fish leads: daily sashimi you can order half-and-half (sea bream cured in kombu or yuzu, herring, flounder), simmered fish with its liver, namerō, oysters from Akkeshi and Seiko crab in season, and in winter a ¥9,000 kue hot-pot course on bonito broth. The sake list is long. Most diners find it good value; one in September 2026 found the portions small, the sashimi thinly sliced and a 3% surcharge on card payments. Closed Sundays and holidays.

chef_bio.background: Per a November 2025 review, the owner is from Saitama. No source names the owner or the chef.

anecdotes.text: "The sashimi platter featured two types: Ishikarei (stone flounder) and Tai (sea bream) with kombu kelp, and I appreciated the option for a half-and-half selection on the menu." — March 2026.
"First, I tried the Kue sashimi… The main dish, Kue hot pot, had an exceptionally refined broth." — December 2025.
"However, I was surprised to find a 3% surcharge for payments made by methods other than cash" — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (公式情報): 純酒肴 吟、文京区湯島3-41-10 コスモビル 2F、上野広小路駅・上野御徒町駅A3出口から徒歩2分、湯島駅2番出口から3分、JR御徒町駅北口から6分、月〜土17:00〜22:00、日祝・お盆・年末年始休み (ほか不定休)、予約可、16席、加熱式たばこの喫煙所、カード・QR可。メニュー (2022年): 炙り穴子刺し850円、天然かんぱち950円、かつおの塩たたき1,000円、刺身盛り合わせ2,000円から、かつおの酒盗500円、へしこ650円。口コミ (2025年11月〜2026年9月): 日替わりの刺身、半々で注文可、ニシン、鯛の柚子漬け、昆布締め、イシガレイ、イワシの煮付け、ウマヅラの煮付けと肝、なめろう、鶏天のカレー塩、厚岸のカキ、セイコガニ、冬のクエ鍋コース9,000円、鍋島1,500円、店主は埼玉出身、2026年9月には量が少なめで現金以外は3%の手数料という声も。

cultural_comfort.note: A small second-floor izakaya with a daily menu; no English menu is listed.

tokyo_mohini_tea_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. Pot tea is the menu; the food is a few cakes and scones, which are wheat-based. Nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_mohini_tea_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Ask. Straight tea is served by the pot; scones come with clotted cream, and milk tea and cheesecake contain dairy.
tokyo_mohini_tea_yotsuya.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 12:00–19:00; closed Monday (Tabelog). Reservations taken (Tabelog). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog; a June 2024 diner paid cash after the meal). 12 seats at six 2-seat tables; non-smoking (Tabelog; January 2026). Tea leaves sold to take home, around 140 kinds (February 2026). Moved here from Akebonobashi in October 2013 (Tabelog).
tokyo_mohini_tea_yotsuya.notes: [Café · Yotsuya, a one-person tea house in a residential alley] A small tea specialty shop on the ground floor of a house down a quiet alley between Yotsuya and Yotsuya-sanchome, with tea canisters lining the walls, jazz playing and six two-seat tables. The owner runs it alone and loves to talk tea: why it should be hot, why water matters as much as for soba or sake, how to brew and how to crush cardamom for chai at home. Each tea comes in a pot of about three cups that deepen as you go, from ¥630, with small scones and clotted cream on the side; around 140 teas are sold by the leaf. One diner warns that it isn't the place for a silent cup: [the owner] talked tea for 45 minutes. Closed Mondays; cash only.

roles: Owner, runs the shop alone (January 2026 review)
chef_bio.origin: Moved from Akebonobashi to the current location in October 2013 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.background: No source names the owner. Reviewers describe a very knowledgeable owner with "a philosophical approach" (June 2025) who "runs the shop solo… passionately teaching the best ways to enjoy tea" (January 2026) and explains each tea to guests (December 2025, February 2026). A January 2025 reviewer calls it a shop certified by the Japan Tea Association.
chef_bio.philosophy: Tea should be served hot; water quality matters as much as for soba, tofu and sake; a pot of three cups because each cup tastes different (2025–26 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The owner runs the shop solo, creating a relaxed atmosphere while passionately teaching the best ways to enjoy tea." — January 2026.
"Just like soba, tofu, and sake, the quality of water is also essential for tea. The reason for the three cups in the pot is that each cup offers a different flavor experience." — December 2025.
"I stayed for about 45 minutes… It may not be the best spot for those seeking a leisurely tea experience, but for anyone interested in tea discussions, it's a must-visit." — February 2024.
"According to the tea expert owner, tea should definitely be served hot." — February 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: モヒーニ 四谷店、カフェ・ケーキ、若葉1-4、四ツ谷駅・四谷三丁目駅から徒歩7分、火〜日12:00〜19:00、月曜休み、予約可、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、12席 (2人掛けテーブル6卓)、禁煙、2013年10月に曙橋から移転。口コミ(2023年〜2026年): 住宅街の路地の一軒家、店主が一人で営む紅茶専門店、紅茶はポットで約3杯分、Mohini 630円、Safari Kenya 630円、Uva 680円、Earl Grey、カルダモンのチャイ、ロイヤルミルクティー、スコーンにクロテッドクリームと自家製りんごジャム450円、ベイクドチーズケーキ、季節のタルト、茶葉の販売は約140種類、Japan Tea Association の認定店という記述。

cultural_comfort.note: Seated and ordered at the table, pay after; the owner explains teas at length, in Japanese in the reviews.

tokyo_tsubame_shokudo_ichigaya.gf_detail: Ask. Lunch plates come with brown rice (or bread on some sets), but bread is baked in house, dinner includes pasta, and sauces are not described; nothing gluten-free is stated.
tokyo_tsubame_shokudo_ichigaya.vegan_detail: Ask. An October 2026 diner had a vegetable-only lunch plate (stewed vegetables, salad, mushrooms, okara and hijiki, brown rice and minestrone-style soup) and called it "almost vegan"; Tabelog lists vegetarian options. Ask about the soup and sauces.
tokyo_tsubame_shokudo_ichigaya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri lunch 11:30–14:00 (last order 13:30) and dinner 18:00–22:00 (last order 21:30 on Tabelog; food 21:00, drinks 21:30 on the website); closed Saturday, Sunday and holidays, plus Golden Week and Obon (Tabelog; website). Weekends and holidays for private hire only (Tabelog). Reservations taken; the ¥2,500 lunch needs a booking, its upgrades by 20:00 the business day before; 100% fee for same-day course cancellations (website; Tabelog). Phone is easiest 18:00–21:00 (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted; à la carte appetizer charge ¥330 (Tabelog). 62 seats over two floors (30 / 32), private rooms for 6 and 8; non-smoking; children welcome (Tabelog). Lunch fills by noon with office workers (2026 reviews). Lunch boxes to take away, by phone (Tabelog). Opened 6 October 2009 (Tabelog).
tokyo_tsubame_shokudo_ichigaya.notes: [Bistro · Ichigaya, a hidden old-house bistro with vegetable-packed lunches] The last house at the end of a narrow alley between Ichigaya and Yotsuya — you won't find it without the sign — renovated into a two-floor bistro with high ceilings, antique chairs and a spiral staircase; the shop says the house was once a writer's bookshop. At lunch office workers queue for the ¥1,200 plate: a daily main such as mackerel nanban-zuke or pork sauté, with salad, vegetable sides, brown rice (refills) and soup, or a vegetable-only version a diner called almost vegan. Dinner is small plates of farm vegetables, house-cured and smoked meats, pasta and Japanese wine by the glass, with free-flow courses for parties. One October 2026 group found it noisy, slow to bring the food menu, small-portioned and pricey, about ¥9,000 a head; another praised the service on a busy day. Weekdays only.

chef_bio.background: No source names the chef or owner. The website: vegetables direct from contract farms, many of them friends of the chef; all meat prepared in the shop's kitchen from grinding, curing and aging to finishing; bread baked in the kitchen; Japanese wines chosen after tasting. The party page describes the building as a renovated house that was a writer's bookshop, available for weddings and space hire.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Ingredients whose makers' faces you can see… dishes that let you feel the four seasons" (website, translated).
chef_bio.specialty: Vegetable-heavy lunch plates; house-smoked meats; Japanese wine.

anecdotes.text: "I ordered the vegetable-only lunch plate… This menu is almost vegan, making it perfect for those looking to reset their bodies or control their calorie intake." — October 2026.
"If it weren't for the sign at the entrance of the alley, I wouldn't have found the restaurant since it's tucked away at the end of a narrow path." — July 2026.
"The food was tasty, but the portions were on the smaller side… The total bill for four people came to just over JPY 9000 per person." — October 2026, dinner.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト: 古民家ビストロ 燕食堂、市谷本村町2-33、市ヶ谷駅から徒歩5分、四ツ谷駅から8分、路地の一番奥の一軒家、ランチ11:30〜14:00 (L.O.13:30)、ディナー18:00〜22:00 (L.O.21:00、ドリンク21:30)、土日祝休み、農家直送の有機・減農薬野菜 (島根県江津市の NAO FARM)、霧島ポーク、青森産鴨肉、北海道産エゾ鹿肉、肉の仕込みから仕上げまで店内で手造り、自家製の天然酵母パン、日本ワインはすべてグラスで、北海道亀田郡の山田農場のガロチーズ、ランチはメイン+サラダ+惣菜2種+三分づき玄米ご飯+スープ1,200円、産地直送2,500円ランチ (要予約)、作家さんの書店をリノベーションした一軒家。食べログ: イタリアン・ビストロ・ワインバー、62席 (1階30・2階32)、個室あり、禁煙、カード・電子マネー・QR可、お通し330円、2009年10月6日オープン。口コミ(2026年): 平日昼は会社員で満席、野菜だけのプレート、ディナーは量が少なめで高めという声。

tokyo_taiwan_yatai_shintaipei_yotsuya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles, gyoza and soy-sauce broths and dressings.
tokyo_taiwan_yatai_shintaipei_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken and animal-stock broths, chashu, braised beef and pork, sausage.
tokyo_taiwan_yatai_shintaipei_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–14:00 and 17:00–22:00 (last order 21:30); closed Saturday, Sunday and holidays, though reserved parties are taken on those days (Tabelog). A January 2025 diner found it closed on a weekday. Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). No service charge (the Tabelog Japanese text says なし; the English machine translation wrongly shows 10%). 25 seats; hire for up to 20 or 20–50; smoking allowed, at lunch too (Tabelog; April 2026). Course dinners with free-flow drinks for groups (May 2026).
tokyo_taiwan_yatai_shintaipei_yotsuya.notes: [Chinese · Yotsuya, a couple-run Taiwanese diner that ramen fans make a pilgrimage to] A plain, local Chinese room with a golden fortune-god statue at the back, in the alley between the Ministry of Defense and Yotsuya, run by a couple — "a father and mother team", as a regular of years puts it. Ramen enthusiasts call it a holy site: the head of the Ganko Ichijo ramen school praised its chuka soba, a salty, deeply chickeny soy bowl with very thin straight noodles. The Taiwanese menu runs to beef noodles (toned down for Japanese palates unless you ask for more heat), Taiwan yakisoba and dan dan noodles, plus fried rice regulars rave about, gyoza and Taiwanese sausage; groups book course dinners with free-flow highballs. Most dishes are about ¥1,000. Smoking allowed; cash only; weekdays only.

roles: Run by a couple (July 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: No source names the owners. "A cozy restaurant run by a father and mother team" (July 2026, a regular of years). A November 2024 diner was asked by a friendly woman on staff whether the beef noodles were spicy enough, and was told the heat is toned down for Japanese customers but can make it much spicier. A golden fortune-god statue at the back "suggesting the restaurant's Chinese roots" (November 2024). Ramen fans call it a holy site, "loved by the founder of the Ganko Ichijo school and featured in the TRY guide" (May 2024); a November 2025 Japanese review mentions the chuka soba the head of the school raved about.
chef_bio.specialty: Chuka soba; Taiwanese beef noodles; fried rice.

anecdotes.text: "It's a cozy restaurant run by a father and mother team. I've lost count of how many times I've visited." — July 2026.
"When ordering, I was asked if I wanted thin or curly noodles… when I mentioned 'Ganko,' [the staff] quickly noted, 'Ah, thin noodles, right?' with a smile." — May 2024.

"[The woman on staff] explained that they usually tone it down since many Japanese aren't fond of spicy food. However, [the woman on staff] also added that if I enjoyed extra heat, they could make it much spicier." — November 2024, Taiwanese beef noodles.

tokyo_mibashou_ichigaya.gf_detail: Ask. The banana juice is bananas blended with milk or soy milk (reviews), but toppings include granola and black cookies, and the hot sandwiches are bread. Nothing gluten-free is stated.
tokyo_mibashou_ichigaya.vegan_detail: Ask. Every juice can be made with unsweetened soy milk instead of milk (Tabelog); a November 2021 diner describes the soy version as just frozen banana and soy milk. Check the toppings.
tokyo_mibashou_ichigaya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 8:00–16:00; closed Saturday, Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). Take-out only since December 2021 (Tabelog; still take-out only in July 2025); 4 counter seats when dine-in ran. Order at a ticket machine; ask the staff for payment other than cash (January 2025). No cards or e-money; QR codes accepted (Tabelog). Stamp card: free toppings at 5 and 10 stamps, a free juice at 15 (April 2024). Daily sandwich and soup posted on Instagram and Twitter the day before (Tabelog). Opened 15 April 2016 (Tabelog).
tokyo_mibashou_ichigaya.notes: [Café · Ichigaya, a tiny banana-juice stand down an alley] A five-tsubo banana-juice shop hidden at the back of a residential alley near Ichigaya Station, marked by a bunch of real bananas hanging outside when it's open. Buy a ticket and the juice is blended to order from bananas and milk or soy milk, with no ice or sugar: thick and shake-like for most reviewers, though one 2022 regular found the premium version disappointingly ordinary. Toppings from granola to yogurt, plus a daily homemade hot sandwich and soup make it a quick lunch, and lines form even on rainy days. Take-out only; weekdays 8:00–16:00. Time Out Tokyo lists a second Mibashou shop.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner. The Tabelog listing, written by the shop, describes a banana-juice specialty shop with homemade hot sandwiches and soups whose daily menu is posted on social media the day before. A March 2022 reviewer explains the name: the Japanese word for banana is "Jitsubashou" (as machine-translated).
chef_bio.specialty: Banana juice with milk or soy milk.

anecdotes.text: "As I got closer, I realized it was a bunch of bananas, a sign indicating that the shop was open." — March 2022.
"Banana Soy Milk Juice JPY 350. Made with just frozen cut bananas and soy milk, it's incredibly rich and creamy." — November 2021.
"Despite being tucked away, it's a popular spot that attracts lines even on rainy days." — May 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗の紹介): ミバショウ、カフェ・ジューススタンド・サンドイッチ、市谷本村町2-33 ART ICHIGAYA #02、市ケ谷駅7番出口から徒歩3分、四ツ谷駅から9分、月〜金8:00〜16:00、土日祝休み、2021年12月からテイクアウトのみ、カウンター4席、カード・電子マネー不可、QR可、2016年4月15日オープン、バナナジュース専門店、氷も砂糖も使わない完熟バナナ350円、「Kan-nyuku-oh Gold Premium」のプレミアム500円、牛乳か無調整豆乳、野菜や果物のカスタマイズ +50円〜、自家製ホットサンド390円、スープ350円、日替わりはインスタグラムと Twitter で前日に告知。口コミ(2021年〜2025年): 路地の奥、吊るしたバナナが営業中の目印、食券機、スタンプカード、行列。タイムアウト東京に「ミバショウ 北千住マルイ」の記載。

tokyo_shunrai_ningyocho.gf_detail: Ask. Small dishes include fritters, kara-age, shumai and spring rolls, and sashimi with ponzu or soy (2024–26 reviews); nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_shunrai_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: fish, chicken and oyster dishes; vegetables are served too, but ask about dashi.
tokyo_shunrai_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 16:00–22:00; closed Sat and Sun (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, including same-day and by email (2026 reviews). Cards and e-money; no QR (Tabelog). 12 seats: 8 at the counter and a private room for 4 (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Opened 14 January 2020 (Tabelog). Run by two women: the proprietress, who chooses the sake, and a female chef (April, May, August 2026); service can feel brisk when busy (March 2026).
tokyo_shunrai_ningyocho.notes: [Izakaya · Ningyocho, a sake counter run by two women] A quiet twelve-seat Japanese counter opened in 2020 and run by two women in kimono and kappōgi: the proprietress chooses the sake and a chef cooks (2026 reviews). There was no sake list in 2020: tell the proprietress what you like and a bottle is chosen for you, leaning to robust, namazake and aged bottles, or leave it to an omakase pairing. The food is small, careful plates made for drinking: kombu-cured fish and chicken, maitake fritters, a single-serving oyster hot pot, and the shumai regulars insist on. A four-seat private room suits business dinners. One March 2026 diner found service brisk when busy. Weekday evenings only.

roles: Proprietress, who selects the sake (2026 reviews)
Female chef ("run by … a talented female chef", April 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Opened 14 January 2020 (Tabelog). "A popular restaurant run by two women" (May 2026); two women in kimono and kappōgi run the counter (September 2026).

"Most of the sake had a robust flavor, and the owner mentioned … selecting them carefully." — August 2026.
"The two proprietresses manage the place, but during busy hours, the service can feel a bit impersonal." — March 2026.

tokyo_hito_8888_ningyocho.gf_detail: Ask. Tempura, croquettes, fried yuba and a carbonara pasta are on the menu (2024–26 reviews); nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_hito_8888_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: sashimi, seafood and dashi-based dishes.

Reservations recommended; online bookings may be moved if they clash with phone bookings; a 2.5-hour limit at busy times (Tabelog; February 2026). Table charge ¥710 (Tabelog). Cards and transport IC; no QR (Tabelog). 10 seats: 3 at the counter and a long table for 6–7 (Tabelog; May 2026). Smoking allowed (Tabelog). Opened 2 July 2018 (Tabelog). The owner runs the place alone, and regulars sometimes help carry dishes (2025–26 reviews).
tokyo_hito_8888_ningyocho.notes: [Izakaya · Ningyocho, a one-man sake den in an old house] A ten-seat izakaya tucked down a lane off Amazake Yokocho in a renovated old house, run single-handed by a cheerful owner since 2018. You pick your sake from a fridge stocked with labels you rarely see, and the owner pours it into a tokkuri. The food is small and careful: thick-cut sashimi, fried yuba with crab cream, dashimaki tamago, and a carbonara regulars keep recommending. Regulars set the tone and even help carry plates, which charms most visitors (2025–26). One October 2025 diner found the simmered fish collar overcooked and the sauce thin, and another thought drink prices high (July 2025). The name is read "Hito 8888" on Tabelog; one 2024 diner was told "Quattro Eight".

roles: Owner, running the shop alone ("the master, managing everything …", October 2025 review)
chef_bio.background: Opened 2 July 2018 (Tabelog). A diner who had been a regular since opening returned after five years (October 2026). Tabelog reads the name "Hito 8888"; a January 2024 reviewer gives the reading "Quattro Eight".

anecdotes.text: "You get to pick your drink from the refrigerator, and the master pours it into a tokkuri (sake pitcher) for you." — October 2025.

"This restaurant has many regular customers, creating a cozy and welcoming atmosphere where everyone seems to work together to enhance the experience! (Helping with serving dishes and taking orders)" — May 2025.
"The simmered collar was slightly overcooked, and the sauce was a bit too sweet and thin." — October 2025.

tokyo_pizza_tane_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: cheese on most pizzas; meat and seafood toppings.

Lunch first come, first served — leave a name and number and you are called, with waits up to an hour on a Sunday (October 2026); dinner by reservation; allergies in advance; no special anniversary plates; pets on the terrace only, booked ahead; no bicycle or car parking (Tabelog). Cards, transport IC, iD, QUICPay, PayPay and more (Tabelog). 20 seats: 6 at the counter, 6 at tables, 8 on the terrace (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Opened 1 September 2025 (Tabelog).
tokyo_pizza_tane_ningyocho.notes: [Pizza · Ningyocho, wood-fired sourdough pizza in a hotel lobby] A small sourdough pizzeria in the lobby of the SOIL Nihonbashi hotel, opened in September 2025 and quickly famous on social media; the dough comes from Parklet's bakery nearby (October 2026). The crust is long-fermented and high-hydration, with a big, chewy, slightly tangy cornicione, and the toppings change monthly: chestnut and maitake, lotus root with salsiccia, saury with myoga. Lunch is a ¥2,150–¥2,300 set with salad and dessert. Expect a wait at lunch; you leave a number and get a call. Some find the sour crust surprising, and the counter stools high and the room cramped beside the hotel reception (October 2026). Dogs welcome on the terrace.

chef_bio.background: Opened 1 September 2025 (Tabelog). A sourdough pizza specialist using homemade natural yeast (Tabelog shop text); the dough is supplied by Parklet bakery nearby (October 2026 review). In the SOIL Nihonbashi hotel, sharing space with the reception (October 2026).

anecdotes.text: "There’s a Parklet bakery nearby that supplies the pizza dough, so I was able to stop by there while waiting." — October 2026, a one-hour Sunday wait.
"The pizza has a high hydration dough that is fluffy and chewy, which is quite rare." — October 2026.
"…at first, I thought the sourness was from the balsamic vinegar, only to realize it was just the dough itself." — October 2026.

Opened 20 August 2013 (Tabelog).
tokyo_boeuf_aya_ningyocho.notes: [Yoshoku · Ningyocho, a basement yoshoku with a ¥1,300 lunch] A basement yoshoku restaurant near Koami Shrine, open since 2013, where office workers fill every seat by noon. All three lunch sets are ¥1,300 with salad, soup and rice (large free); set B, the favourite, piles a juicy homemade hamburg steak, crisp shrimp fry and a crab cream croquette beside a little Neapolitan pasta, and the hamburg's sauce rotates weekly through tomato, demi-glace, pepper and a Japanese grated-daikon sauce. Everything is cooked to order, so it takes ten minutes or so. One November 2025 diner found it pricey for the portion and slow to turn tables. Weekdays only; evenings run late.

tokyo_horumon_aoki_ueno.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a horumon (offal) and beef yakiniku restaurant.

Reservations taken (Tabelog online slots; a same-day phone booking worked in October 2026); late arrivals may lose the table, and busy times may mean a smaller table. 12 seats; small and smoky (2026 reviews). Non-smoking. Cards and PayPay; no e-money. Children welcome.
tokyo_horumon_aoki_ueno.notes: [Horumon yakiniku · Ueno-Hirokoji, Kameido's offal grill in a 12-seat room] The Ueno branch of Kameido's well-known Horumon Aoki: a tiny, busy, smoky room on the Yushima side of Ueno-Hirokoji where you grill offal and beef over the table. The horumon is the point — small intestine, uterus, heart, tripe, omasum sashimi, tongue base — but the Aoki kalbi, loin and tongue are just as praised. Expect about ¥4,000–6,000 a head with drinks, less with the weekday 16:00–18:00 happy hour (¥110 highballs). Book ahead, or call on the day; your clothes will smell of smoke. Non-meat dishes are few.

chef_bio.origin: Branch of ホルモン青木 亀戸本店; other branches in 赤羽 (opened September 2022) and 下北沢 (Tabelog 赤羽 page).

tokyo_ajillo_ueno_yushima.gf_detail: GF — ask: ajillo itself is oil and ingredients, but it is eaten with baguette or gnocchi, and pasta and fried dishes share the kitchen; nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_ajillo_ueno_yushima.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: vegetables such as broccoli and asparagus can go into the ajillo, but the oils include bonito-flake and shirasu versions and nothing is marked vegan.
tokyo_ajillo_ueno_yushima.hours_raw: Mon–Thu 14:00–1:00 (last order 0:30); Fri–Sat 14:00–3:00 (last order 2:30); Sun and holidays 14:00–23:30 (last order 23:00); hours changed from April 2026; closing days not fixed (Tabelog). Reservations recommended — fully booked on an October 2026 Saturday night. One-drink policy and ¥500 cover, waived for course bookings; ID may be checked for alcohol. Order by QR code (October 2026). 18 seats with counter and standing bar; private hire for 20–50. Heated-tobacco smoking area. Cards, e-money and QR. Opened 29 September 2023.
tokyo_ajillo_ueno_yushima.notes: [Ajillo bar · Ueno-Hirokoji, build-your-own ajillo from 2 pm to late] A lively little bar in Yushima, from the team behind Alvino and CONBU, where each table gets an induction heater and you make your own ajillo: choose one of four oils — the bonito-flake dashi oil is the house recommendation — then add shrimp, mussels, broccoli, mushrooms and more, and mop it up with baguette. There is an all-you-can-eat ajillo course, plus carpaccios, pasta and wine. It opens at 2 pm for daytime drinking and runs to 1 am (3 am Fridays and Saturdays). Book for evenings; when it is packed, dishes can be slow — one October 2026 diner waited over 40 minutes for garlic shrimp.

chef_bio.background: Per the Alvino and CONBU Tabelog remarks, the same group runs AJILLO in Ueno, Nakano, Kanda Nishiguchi and Shimokitazawa, plus Alvino, CONBU, Bistronomie Avin and others. No source names the chef.

anecdotes.text: "It's a unique restaurant specializing in ajillo, where each table is equipped with an induction heater, allowing you to enjoy your favorite ajillo." — October 2026.
"I tried the dish with herbs. It was refreshing and light, yet packed with the umami of shirasu (whitebait)." — October 2026.
"It was quite busy, so I understand the delay, but it took over 40 minutes for the garlic shrimp to arrive" — October 2026.

tokyo_tenshin_suya_uguisudani.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: dim sum in wheat wrappers (gyoza, shumai, xiaolongbao, wontons, spring rolls) with soy-based sauces.
tokyo_tenshin_suya_uguisudani.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork, shrimp, chicken, duck and beef dishes; no vegan dish is named.
tokyo_tenshin_suya_uguisudani.hours_raw: Tue–Sat 17:00–23:00 (last order 21:30); Sun 13:00–20:00 (last order 18:30); closed Mondays and some other days — check Instagram (Tabelog). Reservations taken; courses served once the whole party arrives; cancellation charges apply. Children generally not accepted. Charge ¥300 per person. 15 seats (5 at the counter, 10 at tables); semi-private rooms for 6–10. Non-smoking (ashtrays outside). Cards, transport IC and QR. No all-you-can-drink.
tokyo_tenshin_suya_uguisudani.notes: [Dim sum bar · Uguisudani, homemade dumplings and citrus sours] A stylish little dim-sum bar a minute from Uguisudani's South Exit, more Sangenjaya than Uguisudani, with a counter up front and tables at the back. The dumplings are made in-house — chewy pan-fried gyoza with a crisp base, shumai, xiaolongbao, water dumplings — at ¥680 a plate, alongside bigger plates such as braised beef cheek and yu-lin chicken, and a shelf of house citrus sours and natural wines (some sours alcohol-free). Staff explain the menu and pace the dishes well. Tabelog puts dinner at about ¥6,000–8,000 a head. One August 2026 diner, hoping for a gyoza feast, found it more of a date spot. Closed Mondays; no children.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog official listing; an August 2026 review quotes the owner on the gyoza. No source names the owner or cooks.
chef_bio.specialty: Homemade dim sum; house citrus sours.

anecdotes.text: "The 'Homemade, Chewy Pan-Fried Gyoza' is steamed and then pan-fried in a Chinese wok." — August 2026, Mankitsu set.

No reservations; a crowd often waits outside before opening; tell the staff how many, then take the standing counter or a shared table at the back. Popular skewers sell out by evening (October 2026). No appetizer charge, seated or standing. Cash only. 14 seats plus standing. Smoking allowed. Take-away skewers.
tokyo_sasanoya_uguisudani.notes: [Yakitori · Uguisudani, a smoky Showa-era standing bar] A smoke-filled, Showa-era yakitori and motsuyaki bar by the overpass at Uguisudani's South Exit, where people queue before the 15:00 opening. Most skewers are about ¥100: kashira and shiro, chicken, tsukune and offal, with sauce skewers waiting on a grill tray (help yourself to the tare) and salt ones grilled to order, three at a time. Drink cheap sake or shōchū at the standing counter or share a table at the back. Staff explain the system to first-timers. No appetizer charge, cash only, smoking allowed; popular skewers run out by evening; closed Sundays and holidays.
